items.title: D3 data_status is judged only inside a window taken from the bag itself, so a bag that ends early or is missing ACCEPTED still gives 'complete' and pass
items.trigger: (a) The recording stops before the run ends: the record_cap_s timeout fires (480 s; a scenario `timeouts: {nav_wall_s: >~360}` is accepted by config.py and nothing checks it against the cap), the recorder crashes, or someone stops it. stop_record.sh only prints the recorder's exit 124 and still exits 0. (b) The target goal's ACCEPTED/EXECUTING status is not in the bag, and a required stream drops out mid-route.
items.expected: A5: missing key data must stay incomplete. If the recording does not cover the run from the runner's goal acceptance to its stop confirmation, data_status should be incomplete, and so should validation (inconclusive).
items.actual: The analyser window is accept..arrival, and both ends come from the bag: hi falls back to the last odom sample, lo to the first status. A truncated bag therefore has no gap at its own end. The analyser does flag 'goal accepted but no terminal status before the recording ended' and 'ACCEPTED/EXECUTING status was not recorded', but Runner._evaluate only reads data_integrity and drops these flags. The D3 verdict comes out completed/reached/pass/complete.
items.evidence: Ran repro_trunc.py (scratch review-wf/eval, through `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd <scratch> && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 repro_trunc.py"`). It calls the real Runner._evaluate on a stub. The bag stops at sim 3 s while the robot is still driving; status is EXECUTING only. Output: `analyzer: interrupted complete inconclusive ['goal accepted but no terminal status before the recording ended']`, `D3 required_gaps: {'clock': 0.05, 'odom': 0.05, 'tf_odom_base': 0.05}`, `D3 verdict: {... 'task_outcome': 'reached', ... 'data_status': 'complete', 'validation_status': 'pass'}`. Ran repro_noaccept.py: 6 s wall dropout mid-route, only SUCCEEDED recorded. Output: `analyzer: complete inconclusive ["the target goal's ACCEPTED/EXECUTING status was not recorded"]`, clock `count_in_window 61, max_wall_gap_s 0.05`, D3 `data_status 'complete', validation_status 'pass'`. The control run with ACCEPTED recorded gives D3 `incomplete`. With the default limits the cap is not reached (record start to end is at most about 10+300+10+10+90+3 s), so recorded runs are unaffected.
items.fix_direction: Have the evaluator check coverage. The bag's clock and odom must span the runner's accept_sim..stop_confirmed_sim (or terminal_sim), in sim time, from facts. Pass the analyser's coverage flags ('no terminal status in the recording', 'ACCEPTED not recorded', 'target goal not observed') into data_problems. Also treat a recorder exit of 124 as incomplete, and make config.py reject record_cap_s below accept+nav_wall+cancel+stop+teardown.

Output: `A truncated bag (EXECUTING only, bag ends at sim 3.0)`: analyzer `interrupted complete inconclusive ['goal accepted but no terminal status before the recording ended']`, D3 required_gaps all 0.05 -> ('completed','reached','pass','complete','pass'). Control with the same 5 s hole inside the bag -> D3 'incomplete','inconclusive'. `B no ACCEPTED` (3 s dropout mid-route, only SUCCEEDED recorded): clock (count 141, in_window 21, gap 0.05) -> D3 complete/pass; control with EXECUTING recorded -> gap 3.05, incomplete/inconclusive. Extra case v_eval1b.py (recorder died 3 s after start, before the goal; no status/feedback in the bag at all): analyzer `error incomplete ['target goal not observed in the recording', ...]`, but D3 -> ('completed','reached','pass','complete','pass').
verification.reasoning: I checked this against the code at HEAD. In analyze_attempt.evaluate, lo = t_accept, falling back to st[0][0] (lines 243-248) or odom[0] (line 296). hi = t_arr, which falls back to odom[-1] (line 267). So both ends of the window come from the bag, and the part of a run the bag did not capture is never checked. Runner._evaluate (532-556) reads only data_integrity. gap() returns max_wall_gap_s whenever the whole-bag count is >0. The analyser's coverage flags are dropped: 'no terminal status before the recording ended', 'ACCEPTED/EXECUTING not recorded' and 'target goal not observed'. Its own data_status is dropped too: in my 1b case the analyser said 'incomplete' and D3 said 'complete'. The recorder exit code is not checked anywhere. stop_record.sh (115-120) only prints exit codes such as 124. Its exit 6 ('required topic ... 0 messages') is kept in facts.exit_codes but is not an evaluator input. The offline integrity check is the only dropout detector: the live runner never looks for /clock gaps. So a dropout in the unrecorded part of a run would go unnoticed, while A5 says missing key data must stay incomplete. Reachability: default limits cannot hit record_cap_s=480 (worst case about 2+5+10+300+10+10+90 contact-fetch timeout+3 = about 430 s). But config.py validates scenario timeouts only with _positive and never compares nav_wall_s against record_cap_s, and scenario overrides are documented (14.3). A recorder that dies on its own after record_d0.sh's 2 s liveness check also triggers it. No recorded run is affected: no recorded result.json carries these analyser flags, and all 31 stop_record.txt files end with exit 0. Major is justified: a pass/complete verdict with missing evidence, on a plausible fault path rather than the normal path.
verification.fix_direction: Make D3 check coverage. The bag's clock, odom and tf_odom_base must span the runner's accept_sim to stop_confirmed_sim (or terminal_sim/teardown) in sim time. Map the analyser's coverage flags (target not observed, no terminal status, ACCEPTED not recorded) and a non-zero stop_record exit (5/6) or a recorder exit 124 or other failure code into data_problems. Make config.py reject scenario limits whose sum exceeds record_cap_s.

items.title: C1 still holds: a transcript with the sent goal but no goal id is marked verified, and the goal is attributed to the first ACCEPTED/EXECUTING goal in the bag with no caveat
items.trigger: A goal-*.txt that has the 'send_goal start' line but no 'Goal accepted with ID' line (the client was killed or timed out, or the output was lost), with another goal id in the bag: an earlier RViz goal that was still EXECUTING and then got preempted (Nav2 aborts it), or a foreign goal to the same pose.
items.expected: When the target id is guessed from the bag, the attribution should count as uncertain (an inconclusive reason), just as it does when there is no transcript.
items.actual: goal_verified=True. The target is the first ACCEPTED/EXECUTING id in the bag and no inconclusive reason is added. The verdict follows the foreign goal both ways: the preempted older goal gives fail, and a foreign goal that succeeds gives pass.
items.evidence: repro_c1.py output: `A transcript WITH goal id target=aaaa.. verified=True status=SUCCEEDED validation=pass`; `A transcript WITHOUT goal id target=cccc.. verified=True status=ABORTED validation=fail`; `B2 foreign goal + its feedback target=cccc.. verified=True task=reached validation=pass inconclusive=[]`. D3 propagation: none. The runner writes 'Goal accepted with ID' as soon as the goal is accepted (runner.py 361-363). The only runner paths without an id are accept_timeout (runner_errors, so fail) and an interrupt in SEND_GOAL (inconclusive). There the analyser's choice only moves the data_integrity window of a run that cannot pass anyway. Severity is Minor because it affects only the standalone D0 analyser and needs a missing id line.
items.fix_direction: When the transcript has sent_goal but goal_id is None, add an inconclusive reason such as 'target goal id not in transcript; attributed from the recording'. Optionally require a unique ACCEPTED goal within the transcript's accepted_wall/result_wall interval.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/verify-eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 v_c1_c5.py" (section '== C1 / eval-2 =='). Output: `transcript with id: target=aaaa src='transcript' verified=True raw=SUCCEEDED -> reached/pass`; `transcript without id: target=cccc src='first goal id that b' verified=True raw=ABORTED -> unknown/fail` (the foreign preempted goal decides the verdict); `own ABORTED, foreign SUCCEEDED, no id: target=cccc -> reached/pass inc=[]`.
verification.reasoning: Lines 226-230 set goal_verified=True whenever sent_goal is parsed, whatever goal_id holds. Lines 236-239 then take the first ACCEPTED/EXECUTING id in the bag and add no inconclusive reason. The attribution uncertainty shows only in target_goal.id_source and other_goal_ids_in_recording. So a foreign goal can decide the analyser verdict either way. D3 propagation: none that changes a verdict. The runner's Transcript writes 'Goal accepted with ID' at acceptance (runner.py 361-363). The runner paths without an id are rejection (analyser rejected=True), accept_timeout (runner error, so fail), an interrupt in SEND_GOAL (inconclusive) and an exception (error). In those paths the target choice only moves the integrity window. The D0 send_goal.sh flow needs a CLI client killed before its acceptance line is printed. Minor is right.
verification.fix_direction: When sent_goal is present and goal_id is None, add an inconclusive reason such as 'target goal id not in the transcript; attributed from the recording'. Optionally also require a unique ACCEPTED id between accepted_wall and result_wall.

items.title: C2 holds and reaches D3 only for short windows: completeness uses the whole-bag count, and a stream silent across the whole accept..arrival window is reported with a gap equal to the window
items.trigger: A required stream (e.g. /clock) has messages in the bag but none between accept and arrival, and the window is at most dropout_wall_s (2 s wall). Example: accept at 1.0 s, SUCCEEDED at 1.5 s, stop confirmed at 2.5 s, RTF 1, one /clock message at 10 s.
items.expected: A required stream with count_in_window == 0 is missing data in the judged interval, so it should be incomplete. A gap should also be measured from the last message before lo to the first after hi, not clamped to the window edges.
items.actual: The analyser gives clock `{'count': 1, 'count_in_window': 0, 'max_wall_gap_s': 1.5}` with data complete and pass. Runner._evaluate's gap() tests v.get('count'), the whole-bag count, so it passes 1.5 s to the evaluator, and D3 gives pass/complete.
items.evidence: repro_c2.py output: `analyzer: complete pass`, `D3 required_gaps: {'clock': 1.5, ...}`, `D3 verdict: {... 'data_status': 'complete', 'validation_status': 'pass'}`. In the recorded runs the shortest accept..result window is about 10 s wall (cancel runs, plus about 3 s of stop hold at RTF ~0.32). A silent stream would show a gap over 2 s there and be flagged, so no recorded verdict is affected.
items.fix_direction: In stream_integrity, add the last sample before lo and the first after hi to the gap computation. In both the analyser and gap(), treat count_in_window == 0 as 'no data'.

verification.repro: v_c1_c5.py section '== C2 / eval-3 ==' (same command as eval-2). RTF 1, accept 1.0 s, SUCCEEDED 1.5 s, a single /clock at 10 s: `analyzer clock integ: {'count': 1, 'count_in_window': 0, 'max_wall_gap_s': 1.5, 'backward_stamps': 0} stop confirmed -> complete pass`, `D3 required_gaps {'clock': 1.5, 'odom': 0.05, 'tf_odom_base': 0.05} -> ('completed','reached','pass','complete','pass')`. Related edge-clamping case: a /clock dropout from sim 0.0 to 3.8 s that straddles acceptance at 1.9 s is measured as `max_wall_gap_s 1.9` -> complete.
verification.reasoning: stream_integrity (201-208) bounds the gap search by lo and hi and returns the whole-bag count. evaluate (300-302) flags 'no messages' only when count==0. Runner gap() (537-539) also tests the whole-bag v.get('count'). A stream silent across the whole window is therefore reported with a gap equal to the window, and a gap that straddles lo or hi is cut at the edge. Reachability on this machine: whenever the bag shows a confirmed stop, the window includes at least 1 s sim of stop hold. At the measured RTF of 0.32-0.42 that is 2.4-3.1 s wall, above the 2 s dropout threshold, so a fully silent stream is flagged. The recorded unreachable run's accept-to-result time was 48.9 s wall. D3 is affected only at RTF >= ~0.5 or with very short windows, and by the smaller straddle under-measurement. Minor is right.
verification.fix_direction: Treat count_in_window == 0 as 'no data' for a required stream, both in the analyser and in Runner gap(). Compute gaps from the last sample before lo to the first sample after hi instead of cutting them at the window edges.

items.title: C3 holds in the analyser: when odom stops early, arrival uses a stale sample and the tolerance 'fail' outranks 'data incomplete'
items.trigger: /chassis/odom stops being recorded at sim 2.0 s (robot at x = 1.0). The other streams and the SUCCEEDED at 4.0 s continue, so stop-still is not_observed.
items.expected: When the arrival sample is older than the arrival event (or data is incomplete), the position check should be inconclusive, not a navigation failure.
items.actual: arrival_check event=terminal_status, sim_time_s 1.98 (the terminal status was at 4.0), error 1.008 m, so validation=fail ('position error 1.008 m > tolerance'). The data-incomplete reason is only inconclusive and fail wins. Fresher sources in the same result (tf and feedback) put the robot at x=2.0.
items.evidence: repro_c3.py output: `stop_still: not_observed | arrival: {'source': 'sim_state_odom_plus_spawn', 'event': 'terminal_status', 'sim_time_s': 1.983..., 'error_to_goal_m': 1.008...}`, `analyzer: unknown incomplete fail {'fail': ['position error 1.008 m > tolerance 0.5 m ...'], 'inconclusive': ['data incomplete: odom: gap of 6.05 s wall > 2.0 s', ...]}`. D3 propagation: the verdict is unaffected, because it uses sim_control ground truth and the live stop. Output: `D3 ... 'data_status': 'incomplete', 'validation_status': 'inconclusive'`. But the stale 1.008 m arrival_check stays at the top level of the final result.json (see eval-12).
items.fix_direction: Reject an arrival sample whose sim stamp is more than a small bound (e.g. max_stop_gap) before the arrival event: report 'no fresh arrival sample' as inconclusive, and do not add the position fail reason when the source stream is flagged incomplete.

verification.repro: v_c1_c5.py section '== C3 / eval-4 ==' (same command). Odom stops at sim 2.0 s, other streams continue, SUCCEEDED at 4.0 s: `stop: not_observed arrival: {'event': 'terminal_status', 'sim_time_s': 1.9833, 'error_to_goal_m': 1.0083}`, `tf_map_base at arrival x: 2.0 feedback at arrival x: 2.0`, `analyzer: unknown incomplete fail {'fail': ['position error 1.008 m > tolerance 0.5 m (sim_state_odom_plus_spawn)'], 'inconclusive': ['data incomplete: odom: gap of 6.05 s wall > 2.0 s', 'stop-still could not be observed ...']}`.
verification.reasoning: at() (line 272) returns the last sample at or before t_arr, with no bound on its age, so a sample 2 s sim older than the arrival event is used. Lines 317-318 add a fail reason on that stale error. Lines 327-328 rank fail above the data-incomplete inconclusive reason. So a recording fault in the standalone analyser is reported as a navigation failure, against A5's rule that missing key data stays unknown/incomplete. The D3 verdict is unaffected: it uses sim_control ground truth and the live stop. But this stale arrival_check stays at the top level of result.json (see eval-12). The report uses evaluator.arrival_error_m, so the HTML report is not affected. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Reject an arrival sample whose sim stamp is more than about max_stop_gap before the arrival event, and report it as inconclusive ('no fresh arrival sample'). Do not add the position fail reason when the source stream is flagged incomplete.

items.title: C4 holds: odom->base_link samples received before the first map->odom are composed with that later transform
items.trigger: The first /tf map->odom arrives after the first odom->base_link samples. AMCL publishes with gaps of about 2.3-2.5 s, so this can happen at the start of a recording.
items.expected: Samples with no map->odom at or before their receive time should have no map pose (or be marked as extrapolated).
items.actual: j stays 0, so map_odom[0] is applied even when its receive time is later than t_ns.
items.evidence: repro_c4.py (map->odom first received at t=3 s): `odom->base_link received t=0 s -> map x=1.0 (uses map->odom received at 3 s)`, and the same for t=1 and t=2. After t=3 the lookup is correct. Impact is informational only: tf_map_base_link feeds positions and position_source_crosscheck, not arrival_check (sim_state or nav2 source) and not the D3 verdict. In the D4 runs about 20 map->odom messages come before accept, so the recorded crosschecks are unaffected.
items.fix_direction: Skip (or flag) odom_base samples with t_ns < map_odom[0][0].

verification.repro: v_c1_c5.py section '== C4 / eval-5 ==' (same command). map->odom first received at t=3 s with x=1: `odom->base recv t=0 s -> map x=1.0`, same for t=1 and t=2. Those samples are composed with a transform received later.
verification.reasoning: In compose_map_base (116-126), j starts at 0 and only moves forward while map_odom[j+1] is at or before t_ns. Nothing checks map_odom[0][0] <= t_ns, so samples received before the first map->odom get a future transform. The effect is informational only: tf_map_base_link feeds positions and position_source_crosscheck, not arrival_check (the runner always passes --spawn, so the source is sim_state) and not the D3 verdict. It matters only when AMCL's first map->odom comes after goal acceptance. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Skip or flag odom->base_link samples with t_ns < map_odom[0][0] (no map pose yet).

items.title: C5 holds, and the D3 evaluator has the same NaN fail-open: NaN passes comparisons, so goal checks and tolerance checks are skipped
items.trigger: Analyser: `--goal 2 0 nan` (argparse type=float accepts 'nan') against a transcript with yaw 0, or a transcript with yaw=nan. Evaluator: ground truth (x, y) NaN (e.g. an exploded physics state returned by get_entity_state), or a config goal of `.nan` (config.py does float() without an isfinite check).
items.expected: Non-finite goal or ground-truth values should raise an error or give inconclusive, never verified/pass.
items.actual: Analyser: no GoalMismatch, verified=True, pass. With `--goal nan 0 0` the result is verified=True and inconclusive. Evaluator: err=NaN, so `err > tol` is False and the outcome is reached/pass. In the unreachable branch `err <= tol` is False, so the goal counts as not reached and the result is unreachable/pass.
items.evidence: repro_c5.py: `--goal (2.0, 0.0, nan) vs sent (2.0, 0.0, 0.0): no GoalMismatch; verified=True ... validation=pass`; `sent yaw nan vs --goal yaw 0: True pass`. repro_new.py: `N1 ground truth NaN at the stop ...: 'task_outcome': 'reached', ... 'validation_status': 'pass'`; `N1b NaN goal ...: ... 'pass'`; `N1c unreachable preset, ABORTED, gt NaN: 'task_outcome': 'unreachable', ... 'pass'`. send_goal.sh already rejects non-finite values (line 19), so the analyser case needs a hand-given --goal or transcript. D3 does not use yaw.
items.fix_direction: Validate with math.isfinite: --goal and sent_goal in the analyser, goal coordinates in config.py, and gt_at_stop in the evaluator. A non-finite err should give an inconclusive reason.

verification.repro: v_c1_c5.py section '== C5 / eval-6 ==' (same command). Output: `--goal (2.0, 0.0, nan) vs sent (2,0,0): no GoalMismatch; verified=True err=0.0 -> reached/pass`; `--goal (nan, 0.0, 0.0) ...: no GoalMismatch; verified=True err=nan -> unknown/inconclusive`; `argparse accepts: [2.0, 0.0, nan]`; evaluator `SUCCEEDED gt NaN: ('reached','complete','pass',(),())`; `preset unreachable ABORTED gt NaN: ('unreachable','complete','pass',(),())`; also `tolerance NaN, gt 5 m off: ('reached','complete','pass')`, `dropout NaN, gap 9 s: ('reached','complete','pass')`, `config._positive(nan): nan`, `yaml .nan -> {'x': nan}`.
verification.reasoning: All NaN comparisons in analyze_attempt line 228, and in evaluator lines 138, 144 and 116, evaluate False, so the checks are skipped. The repo has no isfinite checks (grep), and sim_adapter.entity_state does not validate its values. In the analyser, a NaN x or y gives only inconclusive, and a NaN yaw gives pass. Yaw is not assessed, so that pass is still right on position, though 'verified' is wrong. The evaluator case is a real fail-open, but hard to reach. NaN ground truth from exploded physics would also make the odom twist NaN, so the stop is never confirmed and stop_timeout makes the run an error. Also, send_goal.sh rejects non-finite values (line 19). One addition: config._positive accepts NaN because NaN <= 0 is False. A `.nan` position_tolerance_m or dropout_wall_s in the config therefore makes every SUCCEEDED run reach and every gap pass. Minor, because it needs bad input or a bad config.
verification.fix_direction: Check values with math.isfinite: --goal and the transcript's sent_goal in the analyser, goal and threshold values in config.py (_positive should reject NaN and inf), and gt_at_stop and err in the evaluator (a non-finite value gives an inconclusive reason).

items.title: In a preset scenario, 'unreachable' rests on a boolean label only: any abort error_code, any rejection, and a scenario with no evidence all give unreachable + pass
items.trigger: A scenario with `preset_unreachable: true` and Nav2 ABORTED with error_code 202 (TF_ERROR) or 201 (INVALID_PLANNER), or a rejected goal. Or a scenario with `preset_unreachable: true` and no `evidence` key.
items.expected: A5 says aborts and rejections must not all be read as unreachable, and unknown causes stay 'unknown'. The docs (technical-overview 14.4 and the evaluator docstring) say unreachable requires 'offline evidence'. The scenario's own expectation is 'ABORTED (error_code 208 or 207 expected)'.
items.actual: The evaluator ignores error_code and the cause of a rejection. EvalInputs has no evidence field, and config.py accepts preset_unreachable with evidence=''. Every one of these cases gives unreachable/pass.
items.evidence: repro_unreach.py: `ABORTED 202 TF_ERROR -> unreachable / pass`, `ABORTED 201 INVALID_PLANNER -> unreachable / pass`, `REJECTED (no error code) -> unreachable / pass` (the recorded 208 case is also unreachable/pass). The codes were checked against /opt/ros/jazzy/share/nav2_msgs/action/ComputePathToPose.action: 201 INVALID_PLANNER, 202 TF_ERROR, 207 TIMEOUT, 208 NO_VALID_PATH. repro_evidence.py: the modified config loads with `preset_unreachable = True evidence = ''`, and an ABORTED run with gt 5.9 m short gives `unreachable pass`. All recorded unreachable runs had error_code 208, so the recorded verdicts are unaffected.
items.fix_direction: Add an expected_error_codes list (e.g. [207, 208]) to the scenario, and give unreachable only for ABORTED with one of those codes. items.actual: `reached = err is not None and err <= tol` is False when err is None, so the outcome is unreachable and the validation pass.
items.evidence: repro_new.py: `N2 unreachable preset, REJECTED, no ground truth at all: 'task_outcome': 'unreachable', ... 'validation_status': 'pass'`; `N2b unreachable preset, ABORTED, no ground truth: ... 'pass'`. On the runner's ABORTED path, ground truth at the stop is always read, and a failure there is a runner error, so only the rejected+teardown-read-failure path is reachable.

I keep Major because interrupts are an advertised D2 feature, the window is about 5 s of every run, fixing runner-2 makes it reachable by a plain Ctrl-C, and the result is an unsupervised goal plus a false 'goal cancelled' exit code.
verification.fix_direction: Check self.interrupt and fsm.check() immediately before send_goal_async and do not send when either fires. Once a goal has been sent, never leave SEND_GOAL unresolved: test fut.done() before the interrupt and deadline checks, wait (bounded) for the response, and if it is accepted go EXECUTING -> CANCELING -> STOP_CONFIRM. If the response is unknown, send a cancel-all and treat an unconfirmed stop as abort_batch (31). Add fake-node cases for SIGINT during the recorder start and for a slow recorder start.

items.title: Ctrl-C in the terminal never reaches the runner: timeout without --foreground puts python in a background process group
items.trigger: Run the documented command `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l .../run_scenario.sh normal`, then press Ctrl-C during the run.
items.expected: README line 41 says '20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断(已取消目标并收尾)'. docs/setup.md line 81 says 'Ctrl-C 只会让它取消目标并照常收尾'. technical-overview §14.3 says EXECUTING '响应 Ctrl-C'. So Ctrl-C should make the runner cancel the goal and tear down.
items.actual: GNU timeout (without --foreground) calls setpgid(0,0). timeout and the python runner are then in a process group that is not the terminal's foreground group. The tty's SIGINT goes only to the non-interactive wrapper bash, which waits for its child. The runner keeps going to the end of the run and exits normally. Two consequences: the documented operator interrupt does not work, and exit 20 cannot be produced from the documented entry. The recorded D2 interrupt evidence (artifacts/d2/commands.md line 33) used a scratchpad script that signalled the PID directly, and test_runner_fake.sh uses `kill -INT "$pid"`, so this path was never exercised. run_batch.sh line 16 uses the same pattern, so batch.py's 'SIGINT stops the batch after the current attempt' cannot be triggered from the terminal either.
items.evidence: pty_ctrl_c.py runs a copy of the wrapper's shape (scenario_like.sh: a non-interactive script ending in `timeout ${FG} -s INT -k 5 30 python3 fake_runner.py`) on a new pseudo-terminal and writes ^C to the master after 1.5 s. fake_runner.py installs a SIGINT handler like Runner.run(). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/runner && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 pty_ctrl_c.py". Output without --foreground (as run_scenario.sh): 'pid=6351 pgid=6350 sid=6349 tty_fg_pgrp=6349 / signal received: none after 6.0 s / terminal output: ^Cscript: timeout exit 0'. Output with --foreground: 'signal received: ['SIGINT', 'SIGINT'] after 1.5 s'.
items.fix_direction: Either use `timeout --foreground`, or start the runner in the background and forward signals (`trap 'kill -INT $pid' INT TERM; timeout ... & pid=$!; wait $pid; wait $pid`). Apply the same change to run_batch.sh. Add a check that sends ^C through a pty to the real wrapper, or correct README/setup/technical-overview.

verification.repro: My own copy of run_scenario.sh lines 10-20 (ROS env sourcing removed, python module replaced by fake_runner2.py, which installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers like Runner.run) runs as `bash -l wrapper_copy.sh normal` on a new pty, and ^C is written to the master after 1 s: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/verify-runner && python3 pty_test.py". Output as shipped (no --foreground): 'runner pid=8150 pgid=8149 ppid=8149 ... sid=8143 tty_foreground_pgrp=8143 / runner signals: none at 5.01 s'. With --foreground: 'pgid=8161 ... tty_foreground_pgrp=8161 / runner signals: ['SIGINT'] at 1.00 s'. GNU coreutils timeout 9.4.
verification.reasoning: Without --foreground, GNU timeout calls setpgid(0,0). The runner is then in timeout's process group (8149), not in the tty foreground group (8143, the non-interactive login bash). The line discipline sends ^C only to the foreground group. That bash does not use job control, so it waits for its child and ignores the SIGINT because the child did not die of it. run_batch.sh:16 uses the same pattern, so batch.py's SIGINT handler cannot be reached from the terminal either. README:41 ('20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断'), setup.md:81 ('Ctrl-C 只会让它取消目标并照常收尾') and technical-overview:403/439 therefore describe behaviour the documented PowerShell entry does not deliver. The recorded D2 interrupt (artifacts/d2/commands.md, 'scratchpad interrupt_demo2.sh') and test_runner_fake.sh:49 (kill -INT "$pid") both signal the PID directly, so the terminal path was never exercised. One assumption remains: my pty emulates how wsl.exe relays a Windows console (Ctrl-C written as 0x03 to the Linux pty). I did not test from a real Windows console, because this session has none. Not unsafe: the run finishes under its own deadlines. But the documented operator interrupt and exit 20 do not work from the documented entry, which misleads on a plausible path.
verification.fix_direction: Use `timeout --foreground ...` in run_scenario.sh and run_batch.sh. Note that --foreground stops the -k kill from reaching grandchildren, which is acceptable because the runner starts its scripts in their own sessions. Alternatively, run the child in the background and forward INT/TERM to it with a trap. Add a pty-based check that sends ^C through the real wrapper shape, or correct README, setup.md and technical-overview.

items.title: An internal error after the goal is accepted tears down with no cancel and no stop confirmation, and exits 30 so the batch continues
items.trigger: Any exception after the goal is accepted (EXECUTING, CANCELING or STOP_CONFIRM before confirmation). The most direct trigger: the dropout pause injection's sim_control call raises SimControlError ('no response within 15 s', service unavailable). Others: OSError writing the transcript, or an rclpy exception while spinning.
items.expected: A5: '检查取消请求已发出还不够，需要观察目标结束状态和机器人速度…停止未确认时，中止后续批次并留下错误'. With a goal still active and no stop confirmed, the runner should cancel the goal, try to confirm the stop, and return 31 (abort_batch) if it cannot.
items.actual: run()'s except calls fsm.fail, which goes straight to TEARDOWN. No cancel_goal_async is sent, no stop check runs, abort_batch stays False, and the exit is 30. batch.py aborts only on 31, so it starts the next attempt while Nav2 was driving the robot through teardown.
items.evidence: repro_3.py (same harness). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/runner/repro_3.py". Output: 'runner exit: 30; states: ... EXECUTING -> TEARDOWN[failure: internal error: SimControlError: /set_simulation_state: no response within 15.0 s] -> DONE; abort_batch: False; goals at the fake Nav2: ['executing'] | cancel requests: 0; robot still commanded to move 10 s after the runner exited: True | stop confirmed: False'.
items.fix_direction: In the error path, if a goal was accepted and has no terminal status: send the cancel, then run CANCELING/STOP_CONFIRM with their deadlines as a best effort. Set abort_batch (exit 31) whenever an accepted goal ends without a confirmed stop.

verification.repro: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/verify-runner/run_all.sh repro_3.py -> 'runner exit: 30; states: ... EXECUTING -> TEARDOWN[failure: internal error: SimControlError: /set_simulation_state: no response within 15.0 s] -> DONE; errors: [...] | abort_batch: False; goals at the fake Nav2: ['executing'] | cancel requests: 0; stop confirmed: False'.
verification.reasoning: Code at HEAD: run() catches everything at runner.py:175-177 and calls fsm.fail, which goes straight to TEARDOWN (runner_fsm.py:140-143) without setting abort_batch. _teardown never calls cancel_goal_async and never runs a stop check. An exception after acceptance therefore leaves the goal running with no stop confirmed and exits 30. A5 says '停止未确认时，中止后续批次'; batch.py:61 aborts only on 31, so a batch continues. I downgrade to Minor because the trigger is an edge case. For scenarios without 'inject' (normal, bypass and unreachable, the default batch), _inject returns at line 372 and nothing after acceptance calls sim_control. Only the dropout scenario's set_state calls, or rare I/O and rclpy errors, can raise. No recorded run has a runner 'error' event or any SimControlError (grep over artifacts/ found none). The A5 gap itself is real.
verification.fix_direction: In the exception path, if goal_id is set and there is no 'terminal' fact, send cancel_goal_async and run CANCELING/STOP_CONFIRM with their deadlines as a best effort, each guarded. Set abort_batch whenever an accepted goal ends without a confirmed stop.

items.title: _teardown is not exception-safe: one failing step skips stop_record, stop_nav2 and result.json, and the process exits 1
items.trigger: Any exception inside _teardown. Examples: (a) the dropout resume fails because sim_control is down or hung (Isaac stalled during the pause): _inject's resume raises, and the retry at line 472 raises again. (b) contact_client.fetch() raises something other than ContactError (e.g. AttributeError on a non-dict reply). (c) OSError opening a script log. (d) JSONDecodeError on a partial analyzer result.json at line 511.
items.expected: The docstring says 'SIGINT/SIGTERM only set a flag, so the run is always closed out', and technical-overview says '任何阶段出错或被中断都会走 TEARDOWN'. Every started recorder and Nav2 should be stopped, and result.json should be written with the error.
items.actual: The exception leaves _teardown and then run()'s finally. What is skipped: stop_record.sh (recorders keep running up to record_cap_s = 480 s), analyze, stop_nav2.sh (Nav2 keeps running and a later start_nav2.sh refuses with exit 3), go(DONE) and result.json. rclpy is not shut down. main() dies with a traceback, exit 1, which is not a documented code.
items.evidence: repro_1.py case E (same command as runner-1). Output: 'runner exit: none - exception escaped run(): SimControlError: /set_simulation_state: no response within 15.0 s; states: ... EXECUTING -> TEARDOWN[failure: internal error: ...] (no DONE); scripts called: ['record_d0.sh'] (no stop_record.sh / stop_nav2.sh); simulator state at the end: paused; result.json written: False'.
items.fix_direction: Run each teardown step in its own try/except that records the error in fsm.errors and continues. Put stop_record/stop_nav2 and _write_result in finally blocks. Catch broad exceptions around contact fetch and the analyzer result read. Add a fixed-input test with a raising sim/contact stub.

verification.repro: Independent: run_all.sh v456.py (real Runner._teardown with fakes). 'runner-4a: teardown with a pending injected pause whose resume raises / exception escaped _teardown: SimControlError: /set_simulation_state: no response within 15.0 s / scripts run: []; final state TEARDOWN; result.json exists False'. 'runner-4d: analyzer left a truncated result.json / exception escaped _teardown: JSONDecodeError / scripts run: ['stop_record.sh', 'analyze_attempt.sh', 'stop_nav2.sh']; final state DONE; runner section in result.json: False'. The copied repro_1.py case E also shows 'exception escaped run() ... scripts called: ['record_d0.sh'] ... simulator state at the end: paused; result.json written: False'.
verification.reasoning: Confirmed: _teardown has no per-step protection. The resume at 472, script() log opens, and json.loads at 511 can raise, and run()'s finally re-raises. That skips ev.close, destroy_node and rclpy.shutdown, and the process dies with a traceback and exit 1, which is not a documented code; batch.py treats it as an ordinary attempt. Two corrections to the finding. (b) contact_client._call already turns OSError, TimeoutExpired, JSON and KeyError/TypeError failures into ContactError, and isaac_py.ps1 always prints a JSON object, so the AttributeError route is hypothetical. (d) happens after stop_record and stop_nav2 have run (4d output), so only result.json and the exit code are lost. The realistic serious trigger is (a): the dropout scenario with sim_control failing on both resume attempts. That leaves Nav2, the recorders (up to 480 s) and a paused simulator. It is an edge case, and no sim_control failure appears in any recorded run, hence Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Wrap each teardown step (resume, contacts, stop_record, analyze, stop_nav2, result write) in its own try/except that appends to fsm.errors and continues. Always reach go(DONE) and write result.json (fall back to the runner-only result when the analyzer file does not parse). Add a fixed-input test with a raising sim stub.

items.title: The pause injection can leave the live simulator paused when the pause takes effect but its reply fails
items.trigger: The dropout scenario at pause time. SetSimulationState(paused) is applied in Isaac, but SimAdapter.set_state then raises: reply timeout in _call, or the follow-up get_state fails.
items.expected: 'never leave the simulator paused' (the teardown comment at line 471). Evidence should record that a pause was issued.
items.actual: _paused_by_injection = True is set only after set_state returns (383). The exception propagates, teardown sees no pause and never resumes, so Isaac stays paused after the run. The 'inject_pause' event is also never written, because the exception happens while evaluating ev.write's arguments at 381. The goal is also left running, as in runner-3.
items.evidence: repro_1.py case C (fake set_state applies 'paused' then raises SimControlError). Output: 'runner exit: 30; ... goals at the fake Nav2: ['executing'] | cancel requests: 0; simulator state at the end: paused | sim_control set_state calls: [(12.7, 'paused')]' (no resume call).
items.fix_direction: Set the flag and log the intent before calling set_state('paused'). In teardown, if a pause was requested, query get_state and resume when it is not playing. Gate the pause to EXECUTING.

verification.repro: Independent: run_all.sh v456.py -> 'runner-5: pause is applied in Isaac, then the reply fails / _inject raised /get_simulation_state: no response within 15.0 s / sim state paused; _paused_by_injection False; injections [] / after teardown: sim state paused; set_state calls ['paused']; inject_pause event written False'. The copied repro_1.py case C matches: 'simulator state at the end: paused | set_state calls: [(12.7, 'paused')]'.
verification.reasoning: SimAdapter.set_state makes two service calls: SetSimulationState, then get_state (sim_adapter.py:66-72). Either can raise SimControlError after Isaac has already paused. In runner.py:381 the call is evaluated as an argument of ev.write, so neither the event nor the injection record nor _paused_by_injection (383) is written. Teardown then never resumes and Isaac stays paused. The 'error' event's traceback does name the call, so some evidence remains. Needs the dropout scenario plus a lost or late sim_control reply. Rare, so Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Record the intent and set _paused_by_injection before calling set_state('paused'). In teardown, when a pause was requested, query get_state (guarded) and resume unless it is playing.

items.title: A terminal status that arrives during an injected pause gives a false stop_timeout (exit 31, batch aborted), and the pause lasts until teardown
items.trigger: Dropout scenario: SIGINT or SIGTERM delivered during the 6 s pause. Nav2's BT and controller loops answer a cancel on wall time, so CANCELED arrives while the sim is paused. It also happens for any scenario where the pause and the terminal status fall in the same loop iteration: _inject pauses first, then the result is seen. The pause is not gated to EXECUTING (380), so it can also start during CANCELING.
items.expected: The injected pause lasts pause_wall_s (6 s), and the stop is judged on data from the resumed simulation.
items.actual: _confirm_stop never services the resume. With the sim paused there is no odometry, so after stop_wall_s the run gets stop_timeout: execution error, abort_batch, exit 31. The simulator is resumed only in teardown, after 12+ s instead of 6 s. The robot was at rest the whole time.
items.evidence: repro_1.py case D (SIGINT 2 s into the pause; fake Nav2 acknowledges the cancel on wall time; no odometry while paused, as recorded in D3 dropout: '/clock、odom、TF 断流 6.1 s'). Output: 'runner exit: 31; states: ... EXECUTING -> CANCELING[interrupt (SIGINT)] -> STOP_CONFIRM[terminal status CANCELED] -> TEARDOWN[stop_timeout] -> DONE; errors: ['stop_timeout'] | abort_batch: True; sim_control set_state calls: [(12.7, 'paused'), (24.85, 'playing')]'.
items.fix_direction: Keep servicing the resume in CANCELING and STOP_CONFIRM, or resume as soon as the run leaves EXECUTING. Gate the pause start to EXECUTING. Start the stop deadline only once the simulation is playing.

verification.repro: Independent: run_all.sh v456.py -> 'runner-6: terminal status seen while an injected pause is active -> STOP_CONFIRM / _confirm_stop -> False; state TEARDOWN (stop_timeout); errors ['stop_timeout']; abort_batch True; sim state at timeout paused; paused for 10.0 s wall so far (pause_wall_s 6)'. The copied repro_1.py case D: 'runner exit: 31 ... CANCELING[interrupt (SIGINT)] -> STOP_CONFIRM[terminal status CANCELED] -> TEARDOWN[stop_timeout]; set_state calls [(12.7,'paused'),(24.85,'playing')]'.
verification.reasoning: Only _execute calls _inject (395-396). _confirm_stop (425-462) never services the resume. A terminal status that arrives during the 6 s injected pause therefore starts a 10 s stop wait with no odometry: D3 dropout records '/clock、odom、TF 断流 6.1 s'. The result is a false stop_timeout with abort_batch and exit 31, and a pause of 10 s or more. The pause is also not gated to EXECUTING (line 380). The realistic trigger is a signal during the pause, which at HEAD needs a direct kill because of runner-2, or a terminal result in the same iteration as the pause start. The error goes in the conservative direction (error, not a false pass). Edge case, Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Call the resume logic from _confirm_stop as well, or resume as soon as the state leaves EXECUTING. Start pauses only in EXECUTING. Start the stop deadline once the simulation is playing again.

items.title: The accept deadline starts before the recorder start and clock refresh, so the A5 10 s acceptance wait is about 5 s, or 0 s
items.trigger: Every real run: SEND_GOAL is entered before record_d0.sh (4.33-4.90 s in all 30 recorded real runs) and before refresh_clock (up to 5 s when /clock stalls). A recorder start longer than 10 s (its own limit is 60 s; record_d0.sh's register loops can wait up to about 32 s) fires accept_timeout on the first check after sending.
items.expected: A5: 目标接受最多等待 10 秒现实时间, measured from sending the goal.
items.actual: deadline_exceeded(SEND_GOAL) measures from the SEND_GOAL entry. In real runs, acceptance gets about 5 s of the 10 s. With a slow recorder start it gets 0 s: accept_timeout, exit 30, and the sent goal is abandoned (runner-1).
items.evidence: phases.py over all artifacts/**/events.jsonl (SEND_GOAL state -> goal_sent): real runs 4.33-4.90 s (e.g. 'normal-20260930-021122 | SEND_GOAL->goal_sent 4.33 | rec 4.33 | sent->accepted 0.002'). repro_1.py case B: record_d0.sh 10.5 s -> 'TEARDOWN[accept_timeout]', exit 30.
items.fix_direction: Start the accept deadline when the goal is sent (reset the entry time or add a sub-state), and give the recorder start its own bound.

verification.repro: phases.py (reads artifacts/**/events.jsonl): in all 31 real runs SEND_GOAL->goal_sent is 4.33-4.90 s, almost all of it record_d0.sh, and sent->accepted is 0.001-0.005 s (e.g. 'normal-20260930-021122 | SEND_GOAL->goal_sent 4.33 | rec 4.33 | sent->accepted 0.002'). Independent v1_sendgoal.py case 2 (recorder 10.2 s): 'reason 'accept_timeout' ... goal response already received [True]'.
verification.reasoning: The accept deadline is measured from the SEND_GOAL entry (runner_fsm.py:73 with fsm.entered), which comes before record_d0.sh and refresh_clock. About 5 s of the 10 s are used before the goal exists. Caveat: technical-overview §14.3 documents the SEND_GOAL 10 s as covering '开始录制,发 NavigateToPose,等接受', and A5 only caps the wait, so this is not an overrun of A5. The real defects: an accept_timeout blames Nav2 acceptance for a slow recorder start; the deadline check runs before fut.done() is re-tested, so accept_timeout is declared even when the acceptance has already arrived (v1 case 2); the goal is still sent after the deadline has passed, which leads to runner-1; and record_d0.sh's own 60 s limit is effectively 10 s. Normal runs have about 5 s of margin, so Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Give the recorder start its own bound and start the accept deadline when the goal is sent (a sub-state or a reset of the entry time). Test fut.done() before the deadline in the accept loop. Do not send when the deadline has already passed.

items.title: Partial start failures are never cleaned up: recorders or Nav2 that did start are left running
items.trigger: record_d0.sh exits 1 when some recorder is not running 2 s after start while the others keep running (record_d0.sh 71-75), for example a session id not registered within 5 s under load, or tf2_echo failing. It also exits 124 when the runner kills only the bash at 60 s: the setsid recorders survive. start_nav2.sh exits 4 when the wrapper session started but the launch child was not seen within 10 s.
items.expected: Teardown stops everything that was started. stop_record.sh and stop_nav2.sh already handle dead or missing sessions.
items.actual: started['record'] and started['nav2'] are set only on exit 0, so teardown skips stop_record.sh / stop_nav2.sh. The bag and text recorders run until the 480 s cap into the failed run's directory and the bag is never copied. A surviving Nav2 makes every later start_nav2.sh refuse (exit 3), so the rest of a batch errors.
items.evidence: repro_2.py case F (fake record_d0.sh returns 1). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/c/Users/Administrator/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/d--RoboSim-Eval/59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da/scratchpad/review-wf/runner/repro_2.py". Output: 'TEARDOWN[failure: record_d0.sh exit 1]; scripts called: ['record_d0.sh', 'stop_nav2.sh']; started flags: {'nav2': True, 'record': False} -> stop_record.sh called: False'.
items.fix_direction: Mark the component as started as soon as its start script has been invoked (or when record.pids / nav2.pid exists), and always call the matching stop script in teardown.

verification.repro: Copied repro_2.py case F (run_all.sh repro_2.py): 'TEARDOWN[failure: record_d0.sh exit 1] ... scripts called: ['record_d0.sh', 'stop_nav2.sh'] / started flags: {'nav2': True, 'record': False} -> stop_record.sh called: False'. Recorded exit codes: grep over artifacts shows record_start exit 0 in 31/31 and start_nav2 exit 0 in 31/31.
verification.reasoning: started['record'] and started['nav2'] are set only on exit 0 (runner.py:292, 331). record_d0.sh exits 1 when any recorder is missing 2 s after start while the others keep running (record_d0.sh:71-75). On the runner's 60 s timeout, subprocess.run kills only the bash, and the setsid recorders survive. start_nav2.sh exit 4 can leave a live setsid wrapper. None of these partially started components is stopped. Recorders stop at the 480 s cap without the bag being copied, and a surviving Nav2 makes later start_nav2.sh calls refuse with exit 3. Never observed in 31 runs, so an edge case, Minor. Fix-direction caveat: after a start_nav2.sh exit 4 the meta file has no boot_id or wrapper_starttime line (written only at start_nav2.sh:65), so stop_nav2.sh would refuse with exit 5 (stop_nav2.sh:36-42). 'Always call the stop script' is not enough for Nav2.
verification.fix_direction: Mark a component as started once its start script has run and its pid file (record.pids / nav2.pid) exists, and always call the stop script in teardown. Make start_nav2.sh write the ownership line (or clean up its own session) before it exits 4, so stop_nav2.sh can act on it.

items.title: Lost contact events (monitor 'dropped' > 0) are recorded but ignored, so safety can be 'pass'
items.trigger: The Kit contact monitor drops FOUND/LOST events beyond 5000 (contact_monitor.py) and reports 'dropped'. Rare: all 26 recorded fetches show dropped 0.
items.expected: A5: '记录丢失数…缺失关键数据就保留 unknown/incomplete' and '未测量不能当零碰撞'. Safety must not be pass when contact events were lost.
items.actual: _evaluate passes only contacts_measured and found_pairs to EvalInputs, and EvalInputs has no loss field, so a run with lost contact events is judged safety pass / validation pass.
items.evidence: repro_5.py (Runner._evaluate with contacts measured, found_pairs [], dropped 1200, SUCCEEDED, stop confirmed, ground truth 0.1 m from goal, complete integrity). Output: 'contacts dropped: 1200 | evaluator contact inputs: ['contacts_measured', 'contacts'] / safety: pass | validation: pass | reasons: () ()'.
items.fix_direction: Pass the dropped count into EvalInputs and make safety unknown (or fail if a disallowed contact was already seen) when dropped > 0. Add a fixed-input test.

verification.repro: Copied repro_5.py (run_all.sh repro_5.py): 'contacts dropped: 1200 | evaluator contact inputs: ['contacts_measured', 'contacts'] / safety: pass | validation: pass | reasons: () ()'. Recorded fetches: 25 with 'events': 0, 'dropped': 0 and 1 with 'events': 6, 'dropped': 0.
verification.reasoning: contact_monitor.py:34-36 counts found/lost events beyond 5000 in 'dropped'. The runner stores the count (runner.py:487-488), but _evaluate passes only contacts_measured and found_pairs (551-552), and EvalInputs has no loss field. A5 requires '记录丢失数…缺失关键数据就保留 unknown/incomplete' and '接触数据丢失，不能写成安全通过'. Very unlikely in practice: drops only affect events after the first 5000 stored ones, and recorded runs have 0-6 events. It is still a real conformance gap. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Add the dropped count to EvalInputs. Make safety unknown when dropped > 0 and no disallowed contact has been seen (fail still wins), and add a fixed-input evaluator test.

items.title: The goal transcript always records action_client_exit=0, even when the goal was never acknowledged or was abandoned
items.trigger: Any run: accept_timeout, an interrupt in SEND_GOAL, cancel_timeout, or an internal error.
items.expected: In the D0 transcript format (send_goal.sh line 79-81) this field is the real exit code of the action client. The analyzer copies it into result.json as nav2_raw.client_exit.
items.actual: Transcript.end(0) is hard-coded, so every result.json reports client_exit 0 (e.g. artifacts/d3/runs/timeout-20260930-012837/result.json line 44), including runs where no result was received.
items.evidence: repro_2.py case G prints the last transcript line of the accept_timeout run (B), the interrupted run (A) and the stop_timeout run (D): each is 'send_goal end ... action_client_exit=0'.
