items.title: Terminal Ctrl-C never reaches the batch: timeout without --foreground moves the batch out of the terminal's foreground process group
items.trigger: Following README step 3 (wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l .../run_batch.sh ...) and pressing Ctrl-C in that terminal to stop the batch.
items.expected: batch.py documents 'SIGINT/SIGTERM stop the batch after the current attempt' with exit 20. The operator should be able to stop a batch from its own terminal.
items.actual: GNU timeout calls setpgid(0,0) unless --foreground is given. The ^C from the pty is delivered only to the non-interactive bash, which waits for its child. Neither timeout nor the batch receives SIGINT, so the batch keeps resetting and driving the live simulator until all attempts finish or the 4 h cap fires. The runner runs with start_new_session=True, so it does not get the signal either. The same `timeout -s INT -k 120 1500` pattern in scripts/wsl/run_scenario.sh contradicts README line 41 ('20 = interrupted by Ctrl-C'). The D2 interrupt evidence (artifacts/d2/commands.md lines 32-33) used a script that sent SIGINT, not a terminal Ctrl-C.
items.evidence: pty_ctrl_c_login.py runs `bash -l <wrapper>` on a pseudo-terminal and writes \x03 after 2 s. The wrapper uses exactly run_batch.sh's `timeout -s INT -k 1200 14400 python3 child.py`, where child.py only logs SIGINT. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/c/.../review-wf/report_batch && python3 pty_ctrl_c_login.py wrapper_like_run_batch.sh; python3 pty_ctrl_c_login.py wrapper_foreground.sh". Output: 'wrapper_like_run_batch.sh -> ^Cchild: did NOT get SIGINT within 6 s | wrapper exit 0' versus 'wrapper_foreground.sh -> ^Cchild: got SIGINT after 2.0 s | wrapper exit 20'. timeout version: GNU coreutils 9.4.
items.fix_direction: Use `timeout --foreground` in run_batch.sh (and run_scenario.sh), or exec python directly and implement the cap inside the program. Document how to stop the attempt that is currently running: signal the runner's session, or have the batch forward the signal to the runner's process group.

verification.repro: $S/run_pty.sh runs pty_test.py, which uses pty.fork and runs 'bash -l <wrapper>' as session leader on a pseudo-terminal, then writes \x03 after 2 s. Each wrapper runs child.py, which logs SIGINT and exits 20 on it, or exits 0 by itself after 6 s. w_nofg.sh uses run_batch.sh's exact 'timeout -s INT -k 1200 14400 python3 ...'; w_fg.sh adds --foreground; w_plain.sh has no timeout. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash $S/run_pty.sh. Output (GNU coreutils 9.4): 'w_nofg.sh -> child pid=7627 pgid=7626 sid=7619 tty_fg_pgrp=7619 ^Cchild: did NOT get SIGINT within 6 s | wrapper exit 0'; 'w_fg.sh -> ... pgid=7651 tty_fg_pgrp=7651 ^Cchild: got SIGINT after 2.0 s | wrapper exit 20'; 'w_plain.sh -> ... got SIGINT after 1.9 s | wrapper exit 20'.
verification.reasoning: This reproduces as described. Without --foreground, GNU timeout moves itself and the batch into their own process group (pgid 7626), while the terminal's foreground group stays the non-interactive bash (7619). The ^C therefore reaches only bash, which just waits for its child. The documented operator path cannot interrupt the batch: README step 3 is 'wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l .../run_batch.sh', and batch.py's docstring says 'SIGINT/SIGTERM stop the batch'. The same pattern in run_scenario.sh contradicts README line 41 ('20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断') and technical-overview line 439 ('导航中 Ctrl-C → 取消、停车、收尾'). The D2 evidence (artifacts/d2/commands.md, 00:46:34 row) used a script that sent SIGINT. runner.script()'s docstring ('a terminal Ctrl-C must not hit the teardown') shows the design expects a terminal Ctrl-C to reach the runner. One residual assumption: I modelled wsl.exe as a pty whose ^C goes to the foreground process group, and I could not drive a real Windows console from here. It is not unsafe, because each attempt still closes itself out. Major fits: operator control that the docs promise does not work on the documented path.
verification.fix_direction: Use 'timeout --foreground' in run_batch.sh and run_scenario.sh, or drop the external timeout and enforce the cap inside Python. Document or implement how to stop the attempt that is currently running (the runner is in its own session), and correct README line 41 and technical-overview line 439, or the scripts.

items.title: The 'collisions' column shows 0 for runs whose contact data was not measured
items.trigger: Any batch where the contact monitor is unavailable, which gives safety_status unknown. This happened for real in artifacts/d3/runs-diagnosis/normal-20260930-012548 and artifacts/d5/defect3-before/normal-20260930-020110. Starting Isaac without -PythonServer, or a python_server failure, would do the same for every run in a batch.
items.expected: A5 says an unmeasured value is not zero collisions. The evaluator's own reason reads "contact data missing: safety cannot be judged (not measured is not 'no collision')". The per-scenario collisions cell should say unknown/not measured, or count only measured runs.
items.actual: RunRecord.collisions = len(evaluator.disallowed_contacts or []). For unmeasured runs the evaluator writes [], and a missing result.json is hard-coded to 0. summarize() adds these up, so the report prints 'collisions 0' next to 'safety unknown N'.
items.evidence: repro_report.py case A (3 runs with safety unknown) printed: 'A. safety counts: {'unknown': 3} | collisions column: 0'. The HTML row read '| bypass | 3 | inconclusive 3 | reached 3 | unknown 3 | complete 3 | 15.00 s | ... | 0 | ...'. On the real records, repro_real_unknown_safety.py printed 'normal-20260930-012548 safety unknown | evaluator.disallowed_contacts [] ... summarize -> {'normal': ({'unknown': 1}, 'collisions', 0)}', with the same result for normal-20260930-020110.
items.fix_direction: Take the collision count only from runs with safety pass or fail (contacts measured). Show 'n/a (k runs not measured)' otherwise, and never add unknown runs in as zero.

verification.repro: $S/repro_report.py case A: three bypass runs with safety unknown and evaluator.disallowed_contacts [], plus one run dir with no result.json. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 $S/repro_report.py". Output: 'A. safety {'unknown': 4} | collisions column: 0 | row: |bypass|4|inconclusive 3, missing 1|reached 3, unknown 1|unknown 4|complete 3, incomplete 1|15.00 s|reached runs only (3 of 4)||- m|0|0|- m|'. On the real records: 'real normal-20260930-012548 safety unknown | measured False | evaluator.disallowed_contacts []' and 'real normal-20260930-020110 safety unknown | measured False | evaluator.disallowed_contacts []'.
verification.reasoning: The evaluator computes disallowed_contacts(x.contacts, policy) even when contacts_measured is False (evaluator.py 155-158), which gives an empty tuple. report.py line 89 turns that into collisions=0, line 77 hard-codes 0 for a missing result.json, and line 109 adds them up. The per-scenario 'collisions' cell therefore shows 0 for runs where nothing was measured, which is the exact case A5 forbids ('未测量不能当零碰撞'). This has happened for real twice (d3 runs-diagnosis, d5 defect3-before). It would affect every run in a batch where Isaac's python server or the contact monitor is unavailable. The safety column in the same row does show 'unknown', which reduces but does not remove the misreading. Major stands: a wrong displayed value, directly contrary to an explicit A5 rule, on a path that has occurred.
verification.fix_direction: Count collisions only over runs whose safety is pass or fail (contacts measured). Render the count as 'n/a' or 'k of n measured' otherwise, and use None rather than 0 for missing or unmeasured runs in RunRecord and summary.json. Add a fixed-input test.

items.title: A result.json that holds only the D0 analyzer's verdict is reported as the run's final verdict (it can show pass with safety unknown)
items.trigger: The runner dies after analyze_attempt.sh has written result.json but before Runner._write_result merges the D3 verdict. In _teardown, stop_nav2.sh runs in between and can take up to 180 s. Ways this happens: SIGKILL or OOM on the 8 GB machine, a native rclpy crash, or an exception in _write_result/_evaluate. In the batch, the attempt's exit code (1 or a negative signal) is kept only in batch.json.
items.expected: The report should show only the runner or evaluator verdict (D3). A result.json without the 'runner' and 'evaluator' sections should be marked as 'runner verdict missing' and listed among the failures or inconclusive runs.
items.actual: load_runs trusts whatever top-level *_status fields are present. The D0 analyzer marks validation 'pass' even with safety 'unknown' (artifacts/d0d/run-01/attempt-01/result.json). Such a run is rendered as a green 'pass' row and is left out of the 'Failure and inconclusive cases' list.
items.evidence: repro_report.py case B copies the real D0 analyzer result.json into a run dir named bypass-20260930-020000 and printed: 'B. analyzer-only result.json -> bypass pass reached unknown | row class: ok | listed under failures: False | has 'runner'/'evaluator' keys: False False'.
items.fix_direction: In load_runs, require the 'runner' and 'evaluator' keys (or a schema marker written by _write_result). Otherwise use validation 'missing' with the reason 'runner did not finish; only the offline analyzer verdict exists'. Better still, write the merged result atomically (tmp file plus rename) under a new name that the analyzer never writes.

verification.repro: repro_report.py case B copies the real analyzer-only artifacts/d0d/run-01/attempt-01/result.json into a scratch run dir. Output: 'B. analyzer-only -> bypass pass reached unknown | row class ok: True | in failure list: False | keys runner/evaluator: False False | schema: robosim-eval attempt result, D0 (plan doc A5)'. The window is real. In the recorded D4 and D5 runs, the analyze event came 10.5-16.4 s before nav2_stop, measured from t_mono in events.jsonl for 13 runs.
verification.reasoning: The mechanism holds. analyze_attempt.py writes result.json with validation from the D0 expectation and safety 'unknown' (lines 359-361). Runner._teardown then runs stop_nav2.sh and only after that calls _write_result, which merges the D3 verdict and the 'runner' and 'evaluator' sections. load_runs does not check for those sections, so a run cut off in that window renders as a green 'pass' and is left out of the failure list. The batch's rc (-9 or 1) exists only in batch.json, which the report never reads. I downgraded it to Minor because the trigger needs abnormal runner death (SIGKILL, OOM, a native crash, or an uncaught exception in _write_result/_evaluate) inside a window of about 15 s. Python exceptions in the main path are caught, and teardown helpers wrap their own errors (script() catches TimeoutExpired, contacts wraps everything in ContactError). No recorded run shows it. When it does happen, though, it produces a false pass.
verification.fix_direction: In load_runs, require the 'runner' and 'evaluator' keys, or a marker written only by _write_result. Otherwise record validation 'missing' with the reason 'runner did not finish; only the offline analyzer verdict exists'. Better, write the merged result to a separate file atomically (tmp file plus rename).

items.title: The batch keeps driving the simulator after a runner crash or kill, although that attempt never confirmed a cancel or stop
items.trigger: The runner exits with a code outside {0,10,11,20,30,31}: SIGKILL or OOM (rc -9), a native segfault in rclpy/Fast DDS (rc -11), or an uncaught exception in teardown (rc 1) while Nav2 still has an active goal and the recorders are still running.
items.expected: A5: when the stop is not confirmed, abort the rest of the batch and leave an error. An attempt that ended without closing out has, by definition, no confirmed stop.
items.actual: The batch aborts only on rc == 31. The next attempt runs its PREPARE step, which resets and teleports the robot under the orphaned Nav2 that is still commanding /cmd_vel. start_nav2.sh then refuses (exit 3), so every remaining attempt errors after resetting the sim again. The batch exits 0 ('all attempts ran').
items.evidence: repro_batch.py case runner_killed (the first attempt returns -9 and leaves a run dir with no result.json) printed: '== runner_killed: batch exit 0; batch.json attempts=3 exits=[-9, 0, 0] status=0'. Attempts 1 and 2 were started.
items.fix_direction: Treat any exit code other than the documented 0/10/11/20/30 (including negative codes, 1, and a missing or unmerged result.json) as an unconfirmed stop. Abort the remaining attempts with status 31, or run a safety close-out (stop_nav2.sh, stop_record.sh, zero-velocity check) before continuing.

verification.repro: repro_batch.py cases runner_killed and runner_exc. Output: '== runner_killed: batch exit 0; attempts=3 exits=[-9, 0, 0] status=0 | Engineering trial of 3 attempts' and '== runner_exc: batch exit 0; attempts=3 exits=[1, 0, 0] status=0'. $S/cap_test.log (case 2) separately shows that a SIGKILLed parent leaves its start_new_session child running: 'case2: runner pid 8381 still alive after the batch was SIGKILLed'.
verification.reasoning: batch.py line 61 aborts only on rc == 31. A runner that dies abnormally (negative rc, or 1 from an uncaught exception, for example in _teardown or _write_result) has no confirmed stop, and its setsid-started Nav2 and recorders are orphaned. The next attempt's PREPARE resets the sim first (runner.py _prepare then _reset_sim), and only afterwards does start_nav2.sh refuse with exit 3 when Nav2 nodes are visible (start_nav2.sh 27-37). Each remaining attempt therefore resets the sim and exits 30, and the batch exits 0. There is also a subtler case: if a run already had abort_batch=True (stop unconfirmed) and then raised in _write_result, it exits 1 instead of 31 and the A5 abort is lost. I downgraded it to Minor because every trigger needs abnormal termination of the runner, which the recorded runs never show. The runner catches exceptions in its main path, and the teardown helpers wrap their own errors.
verification.fix_direction: Treat any rc outside the documented {0,10,11,20,30} as an unconfirmed stop (abort with status 31), or run a safety close-out (stop_nav2.sh, stop_record.sh, zero-velocity check) before the next attempt. Also check that the run dir holds a merged result.json with a 'runner' section.

items.title: 'mean time (success only)' includes reached runs whose validation failed or was inconclusive

This is real: in artifacts/d5/batch-20260930-021530/runs/report.html the normal_slow mean of 24.08 s includes normal_slow-20260930-021734, which is inconclusive and also listed under 'Failure and inconclusive cases'.
items.expected: A6 says to state whether the average counts only successful tasks. The column header 'success only' should match its basis: either average only validation-pass runs, or title the column 'reached runs only'.
items.actual: The basis is task_outcome == 'reached', whatever the validation. A reached run with a collision (validation fail, safety fail) is averaged under the header 'mean time (success only)', and the summary.json key is mean_accept_to_result_sim_s_success_only. tests/test_report.py only uses a failed run with outcome 'unknown', so this case is not covered.
items.evidence: repro_report.py case C (bypass-0 pass/reached 20 s; bypass-1 fail/reached/safety fail 60 s) printed: 'C. mean 'success only': 40.0 | basis: reached runs only (2 of 2) | header has 'success only': True | bypass-1 in failure list: True'.
items.fix_direction: Either restrict the mean to validation == 'pass' runs, or rename the header and the key to 'reached runs' and state the validation mix in the basis text. Add a fixed-input test with a reached-but-failed run.

verification.repro: repro_report.py case C: bypass-0 pass/reached at 20 s, and bypass-1 fail/reached/safety fail at 60 s with one disallowed contact. Output: 'C. mean: 40.0 | basis: reached runs only (2 of 2) | header 'success only': True | note says 'reached runs only': True'. verification.reasoning: summarize (line 101) filters on outcome == 'reached' only, while the column header (line 212) and the summary.json key say 'success only'. The basis line and the note paragraph do say 'reached runs only', so A6's requirement to state the basis is technically met, and the impact is a label inconsistency. The test test_average_time_is_success_only_and_labelled claims 'the failed 40 s run is excluded', but that run is excluded only because its outcome is 'unknown'. A reached-but-failed run would be averaged, so the test does not cover what its name says. Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Either rename the header and key to 'reached runs' and show the validation mix, or restrict the mean to validation == 'pass'. Add a fixed-input test with a reached-but-failed run.

items.title: The 4 h cap exits 124, which is undocumented and masks 20 and 31; the 1200 s kill-after can SIGKILL the batch mid-attempt and orphan the runner
items.trigger: The batch reaches the 14400 s cap. A worse case: the cap fires while an attempt still needs more than 1200 s. A single attempt can legitimately take that long: teardown alone allows 3+180+300+180 s, plus up to 300 s of wall-clock navigation, 186 s for doctor, 90 s for start_nav2 and 90 s for the contact fetch, and run_scenario.sh sizes one attempt at 1500 s.
items.expected: The header lists exits 0/31/20/2 and says the batch 'stops after the current attempt'. A capped batch should still write batch.json and the report and exit 20, or 31 when the capped attempt was an unconfirmed stop.
items.actual: GNU timeout returns 124 whenever the cap fired, even though the batch itself returned 20 or 31. If the batch has not finished within 1200 s after SIGINT, timeout sends SIGKILL to the batch's process group. batch.json and the report are never written. The runner was started with start_new_session=True, so it is outside that group: it is not killed and keeps running unsupervised.
items.evidence: cap_exit.sh runs `timeout -s INT -k 30 2 python3 child.py`, where the child handles SIGINT and exits 20. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash /mnt/c/.../review-wf/report_batch/cap_exit.sh. Output: 'child: got SIGINT after 2.0 s / timeout exit when the cap fired: 124'.
items.fix_direction: Use --preserve-status, or document 124. Make the kill-after larger than the worst-case attempt. On the batch's own shutdown path, forward the signal to the runner's session and wait for it, so the runner is never orphaned.

verification.repro: $S/cap_test.sh runs fake_batch.py, where SIGINT only sets a flag (exit 20) and the 'runner' is an 8 s child started with start_new_session=True. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -c "bash $S/cap_test.sh > $S/cap_test.log 2>&1". Log: 'case1 (cap 2 s, kill-after 30 s): timeout exit 124'; '... line 7: 8379 Killed  MARK=$PWD/mark timeout -s INT -k 1 2 python3 fake_batch.py'; 'case2 (cap 2 s, kill-after 1 s): timeout exit 137'; 'case2: runner pid 8381 still alive after the batch was SIGKILLed'; 'runner finished on its own'.
verification.reasoning: When the 4 h cap fires, run_batch.sh returns 124 instead of the batch's 20 (or 31). The header documents only 0/31/20/2. Once kill-after expires, timeout SIGKILLs its own process group (itself included, exit 137), so batch.json and the report are never written. The runner, in its own session, survives unsupervised. One correction: the exit in the kill-after case is 137, not 124. The kill-after path needs the current attempt to run on for more than 1200 s after the cap. Recorded attempts take 100-225 s, and only a chain of runner timeouts could exceed 1200 s. The 124 is certain whenever the cap fires, but that needs a batch longer than 4 h (about 80 or more attempts). Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Use --preserve-status or document 124/137. Make kill-after larger than the runner's worst-case close-out. On shutdown, have the batch forward the signal to the runner's session and wait for it.

A regression at batch.py line 61, 49 or 63 would pass the suite. repro_batch.py shows such a test is easy to write without child processes. Minor.

items.title: The docs call the report's map trajectories ground truth, but they are spawn plus ideal odometry, and the page does not label their source

items.title: Usage-limit detection and retry-time parsing scan the whole Codex transcript, which includes the text of the files being reviewed, so a successful round can be counted as rate-limited and the retry time can come from quoted text
items.trigger: Any queued round in which Codex reads a file that contains 'hit your usage limit' or a 'try again at <date>' string. The next item of the live queue does this: round1c-c (codex-prompt-round1c-c.md:17 puts scripts/windows/run_codex_review.ps1 in scope, and line 25 of that file at 19203e0 contains the pattern). The same happens for reviews of run_codex_review_queue.ps1, codex_queue_lib.ps1, test_codex_queue_lib.ps1 and docs/review/2026-09-29-d0/REVIEW.md. codex exec writes the file contents it reads to stderr. Examples: codex-round1c-b-stderr.txt lines 743/797/875/898 contain source lines of start_nav2.sh, stop_nav2.sh and record_d0.sh, and codex-round1b-stderr.txt:3165 contains run_codex_review.ps1 line 25 itself.
items.expected: A round that exits 0 and writes its report counts as done. The retry time comes only from Codex's own final 'ERROR: ... try again at' line.
items.actual: $limit comes back True, so the success test `$rc -eq 0 -and report -and -not $limit` fails. The good report is renamed to codex-<round>-attemptN-report.md and the round is run again, spending scarce quota each time, for up to MaxAttempts (8). Then the queue exits 2 and round1c-d, d1, d2a/b, d3a/b, d4 and d5 never run. run_codex_review.ps1 also writes usage_limit_hit=True into the status file of a successful review. When the limit is real, ConvertFrom-RetryText prefers ANY date-bearing match anywhere in the transcript over Codex's time-only message. If the transcript quotes test_codex_queue_lib.ps1, the queue sleeps until 2026-10-02T13:10 instead of 12:09. If it quotes REVIEW.md (the 'Sep 30th, 2026 3:35 AM' line), it gets a past time, does not sleep, and burns attempts at once.
items.evidence: Repro 1 (scratch review-wf/shell/repro_limit_false_positive.ps1): uses the scripts' own expressions on (a) the real successful round1c-b stderr and (b) the same file plus the lines of `git show 19203e0:scripts/windows/run_codex_review.ps1`. Output: `ok-stderr-real.txt: usage_limit=False counted_as_success=True` / `ok-stderr-with-file.txt: usage_limit=True counted_as_success=False retry_time=none -> 30 min fallback`. Repro 2 (repro_retry_transcript.ps1): transcript = test_codex_queue_lib.ps1 lines + the real round1c-c-attempt1 message 'try again at 12:06 PM.' Output: `-> queue sleeps until 2026-10-02T13:10:00`. With REVIEW.md quoted: `-> 2026-09-30T03:38:00` (already past). The real stderr alone gives `2026-09-30T12:09:00`. The live queue log shows it is sleeping until 12:09 and will then run round1c-c.
items.fix_direction: Classify only from Codex's own terminal error. For example, take the last non-empty stderr lines and require `^ERROR: .*hit your usage limit` together with a nonzero exit and no report. Parse 'try again at' only from that same line. Add test cases where the transcript quotes the pattern and older dated messages.

verification.repro:
Scratch C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\d--RoboSim-Eval\59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da\scratchpad\review-wf\verify-shell\repro_shell1.ps1. It dot-sources the repo codex_queue_lib.ps1 and applies queue line 74 verbatim plus the line 76 success test to four transcripts: (1) the real successful codex-round1c-b-stderr.txt; (2) the same file plus the output of `git show 19203e0:scripts/windows/run_codex_review.ps1`; (3) test_codex_queue_lib.ps1 text plus the real codex-round1c-c-attempt1-stderr.txt; (4) REVIEW.md line 10 plus the same attempt1 stderr. Now = 07:12:36. Command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File repro_shell1.ps1. Output:
 t_ok_real.txt: rc=0 report=True usage_limit=False counted_as_success=True
 t_ok_with_file.txt: rc=0 report=True usage_limit=True counted_as_success=False retry=none -> 30 min fallback
 t_limit_with_testlib.txt: rc=1 report=False usage_limit=True retry=2026-10-02T13:10:00
 t_limit_with_review.txt: rc=1 report=False usage_limit=True retry=2026-09-30T03:38:00 (already past)
verification.reasoning:
The premise holds. codex exec writes each command's full output to stderr. codex-round1b-stderr.txt:3165 is line 25 of run_codex_review.ps1 itself, from a diff, and codex-round1c-b-stderr.txt:743/797/875/898 are source lines of the reviewed scripts. The codex-prompt-round1c-c.md:17 scope includes run_codex_review.ps1, and :8 tells Codex to read it with `git show 19203e0:<path>`. Line 25 of that file contains the literal 'hit your usage limit'.

At HEAD, queue:74 matches the pattern anywhere in the file, and :76 needs `-not $limit` to count a round as done. A successful round is therefore renamed to attemptN-report.md and re-run. Each re-run reads the same file again, so every attempt fails the same way until MaxAttempts is reached, and the queue exits 2 with every later item skipped. run_codex_review.ps1:25 writes usage_limit_hit=True into that round's status file.

ConvertFrom-RetryText (lib:9-20) prefers any dated match anywhere in the text over Codex's own time-only line. The repro shows both effects: a two-day-late retry, and a past time that produces no sleep.

One correction to the finding: the live queue is no longer running HEAD code. At 07:25 it was restarted (pid 35156) from the fix worktree at branch fix/review-round1 @156c31a ('judge Codex usage limits only from its own ERROR lines'). HEAD 7fe517e still has the defect until that fix is merged.
verification.fix_direction: Treat exit 0 plus a written report as done, whatever the transcript contains. Classify the usage limit, and parse 'try again at', only from Codex's own terminal ERROR line(s). 156c31a does this by keeping only lines that start with 'ERROR: '. A filter on line start can still match a stderr file that Codex prints verbatim: codex-round1b-stderr.txt:3504 starts with 'ERROR: You’ve hit your usage limit ... Sep 30th, 2026 3:35 AM'. So prefer the last ERROR lines of the file, and only when rc != 0 and no report exists. Add fixed-input cases for quoted patterns.

items.title: Ctrl-C on run_scenario.sh / run_batch.sh never reaches the runner or the batch, because timeout without --foreground moves itself out of the terminal's foreground process group
items.trigger: The operator presses Ctrl-C in the console running `wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval/scripts/wsl/run_scenario.sh normal` (the documented entry point in setup.md:78, README.md:36) or run_batch.sh. From an interactive console, wsl.exe runs the command on a pty.
items.expected: setup.md:81 says 'Ctrl-C 只会让它取消目标并照常收尾'. README.md:41 says '20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断(已取消目标并收尾)'. technical-overview.md:403/439 says the runner responds to Ctrl-C. The batch should stop after the current attempt with exit 20.
items.actual: GNU timeout (not --foreground) calls setpgid(0,0), so the runner runs in timeout's own process group. The kernel sends the tty SIGINT only to the foreground group, which contains only the script's bash. Non-interactive bash waits for its child and ignores the SIGINT because the child did not die of it. The run goes on to its natural end, no cancel happens, and the exit code is not 20. The same applies to the batch, which never gets its stop flag. The documented D2 evidence did not use this path: artifacts/d2/commands.md:33 ran scratchpad interrupt_demo2.sh, which starts `python3 -m robosim_eval.runner` directly and does `kill -INT $PID`. test_runner_fake.sh:49 also signals the runner PID directly, so no test covers the wrapper.
items.evidence: Repro (no signal sent; scratch review-wf/shell/repro_ctrlc_pgrp2.py runs a copy of run_scenario.sh's last line from a script file under a real pty and prints, from inside the supervised program, its pgrp and the tty's foreground pgrp). Command: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- python3 .../repro_ctrlc_pgrp2.py`. Output: `== bash -l like_run_scenario.sh: script bash pid=6501 pgrp=6501; supervised child: pgrp=6510 tty_foreground_pgrp=6501 same_group=False` versus the --foreground variant `pgrp=6512 tty_foreground_pgrp=6512 same_group=True`. timeout (GNU coreutils) 9.4.
items.fix_direction: Use `timeout --foreground -s INT -k 120 1500 ...`. The runner's script children already run in their own sessions, so losing group-kill is acceptable. Alternatively, run timeout in the background with `trap 'kill -INT "$tpid"' INT TERM; wait`. Do the same in run_batch.sh. Add a pty-based check, or correct setup.md, README and technical-overview.

verification.repro:
No signal was sent. Scratch files: like_run_scenario.sh (the last line of run_scenario.sh), like_run_scenario_fg.sh (the same with --foreground), like_run_scenario_login.sh, and probe_pgrp.py, which prints its pgrp and the tty's foreground pgrp. repro_shell2.py and repro_shell2b.py run each wrapper under a fresh pty, with bash as session leader as under wsl.exe. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- python3 .../verify-shell/repro_shell2.py. Output (timeout GNU coreutils 9.4):
 bash like_run_scenario.sh: script bash pid=7901 pgrp=7901; supervised child pgrp=7906 tty_foreground_pgrp=7901 in_foreground=False
 --foreground variant: child pgrp=7908 tty_foreground_pgrp=7908 in_foreground=True
 bash -l form (repro_shell2b.py): flags=hB (no job control); child pgrp=8647 tty_foreground_pgrp=8640 in_foreground=False
verification.reasoning:
run_scenario.sh:20 and run_batch.sh:16 use `timeout -s INT -k ...` without --foreground. GNU timeout then calls setpgid(0,0), so the runner or batch leaves the terminal's foreground process group. The repro shows this for both plain bash and the documented `bash -l` form. A tty Ctrl-C (wsl.exe passes ^C to the pty) reaches only the script's bash. That bash is non-interactive and has no job control. It keeps waiting, and the runner never sees SIGINT, so it neither cancels nor exits with 20.

The docs claim otherwise: setup.md:81, README.md:41 ('20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断') and technical-overview.md:403. The runner's own script() docstring ('a terminal Ctrl-C must not hit the teardown') shows the design expects a terminal Ctrl-C to reach the runner.

The D2 interrupt evidence (artifacts/d2/commands.md, 00:46:34, interrupt_demo2.sh) and test_runner_fake.sh signal the runner PID directly, so the wrapper path is untested. A4 D2 requires '中断也收尾'. The run still tears down at its natural end, so nothing is unsafe. Major holds because the documented entry point's interrupt does nothing on the normal interactive path.
verification.fix_direction: Use `timeout --foreground -s INT -k 120 1500` in run_scenario.sh and `--foreground` in run_batch.sh. The runner's script() children already use start_new_session=True. Alternatively, run timeout in the background with `trap 'kill -INT $tpid' INT TERM; wait`. Add a pty-based check that the child is in the tty's foreground group, or correct setup.md, README.md and technical-overview.md.

items.title: stop_record.sh sends SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGKILL to the recorded session ids without any ownership check, and PIDs demonstrably wrap on this machine
items.trigger: stop_record.sh runs on an attempt dir whose recorder sessions have already ended, and meanwhile the PID counter has wrapped or WSL has restarted. Example: after a runner crash the recorders stop themselves at the 480 s cap, and later the operator follows setup.md:132 ('若有未停的记录器:stop_record.sh <attempt_dir>'), which is also the only tool that copies and checks the bag.
items.expected: Plan B0 'stop only what you have confirmed you own'. stop_nav2.sh does this with boot_id, wrapper start time and command line, and its header states that run dirs are kept and PIDs are reused after a WSL restart.
items.actual: Any live session whose id equals a number in record.pids gets `pkill -INT/-TERM/-KILL -s <sid>`. That can be the Nav2 wrapper session of a current run (start_nav2 uses setsid), another attempt's recorder, a user shell, or, after a WSL restart, boot-time services. Post-wrap recorder ids are low (816-885 in the 02:22:58 attempt), which is exactly where boot-time processes land.
items.evidence: `cat /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` in the Ubuntu distro prints 99999. A survey of tracked artifacts/*/record.pids shows about 700-1000 pids per run and a wrap during D4/D5: the 02:20:53 attempt has 'bag 99724 ... tf_map_base 99793' and the 02:22:58 attempt has 'bag 816 ... tf_map_base 885'. Static code: stop_record.sh:23 reads the sids, and :24-34 check liveness and signal them. No boot_id, start time or command-line check exists; record_d0.sh records only the session ids.
items.fix_direction: In record_d0.sh, record boot_id and each wrapper's start time. The wrapper command line already contains "$ATT/<name>.exit". Before signalling, have stop_record.sh verify all three like stop_nav2.sh does, and refuse (with a distinct exit code) otherwise.

verification.repro: Static only; I did not run stop_record.sh or record_d0.sh. Checks: `wsl -d Ubuntu -- cat /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` gives 99999. A survey of `git ls-files 'artifacts/*record.pids'` shows about 800-900 PIDs per run and a wrap inside the D5 batch: normal-20260930-022017 has 'bag 99724 ... tf_map_base 99793', and normal_slow-20260930-022225 has 'bag 816 ... tf_map_base 885'.
verification.reasoning:
stop_record.sh:23 reads the session ids from record.pids. Lines 24-34 then run pgrep -s and pkill -INT/-TERM/-KILL -s against each id. There is no boot_id, start-time or command-line check, and record_d0.sh records none of those. This contradicts plan B0 ('仅停止自己确认拥有的进程') and the pattern stop_nav2.sh already uses.

On the runner path, stop_record runs within the 480 s record cap while the recorder sessions are still alive, and PID reuse inside one run is impossible (it would need about 99,999 allocations). The exposure is therefore limited to manual invocation on an old attempt dir after its recorders ended (setup.md:132), or after a WSL restart. There, ids like 816-885 can equal the session id of a boot-time service or an unrelated wsl.exe session, which would then be sent INT, TERM and finally KILL.
verification.fix_direction: Have record_d0.sh record boot_id plus each wrapper's /proc start time. The wrapper command line already contains "$ATT/<name>.exit". stop_record.sh should verify all three before signalling each session and skip or refuse (distinct exit code) otherwise, mirroring stop_nav2.sh:36-43.

items.title: When record_d0.sh fails, the recorders it did start are never stopped; re-running it in the same dir loses track of them
items.trigger: record_d0.sh exits 1 because one of the six recorders is not running 2 s after start, or a wrapper took more than 5 s to write its pid file (record.pids gets 'MISSING').
items.expected: Every recorder that was started is stopped and checked in teardown. The runner docstring says TEARDOWN always runs stop_record.sh.
items.actual: The runner calls fsm.fail and returns before `self.started["record"] = True`, so _teardown skips stop_record.sh. The remaining sessions run until the 480 s cap (record_cap_s). They keep appending to the failed run's odom.txt, cmd_vel.txt and other streams after its result.json is written. In a batch they also record the next attempt's reset and navigation into the failed run's files, running alongside the next bag recorder. The ~/robosim_bags bag is never copied or checked. On the manual D0 path, re-running record_d0 on the same dir does `: > record.pids` and deletes pid-* without checking liveness. stop_record then only knows the new sessions, and old and new recorders write the same <name>.txt.
items.evidence: Static: runner.py:324-331 sets started['record'] only when rc == 0, and runner.py:494 gates stop_record on it. record_d0.sh:72-75 returns 1 while the other sessions keep running. The path is untested: all 31 recorded runs have `"event": "record_start", "exit_code": 0` (git grep over artifacts/*events.jsonl).
items.fix_direction: Run stop_record.sh in teardown whenever record_d0 was invoked and record.pids exists. Alternatively, have record_d0.sh stop what it started before exiting 1. Make record_d0.sh refuse when pid-* sessions in the dir are still alive.

verification.repro: Static only; record_d0.sh may not be run here. I confirmed that runner.py:324-331 sets started['record'] only after `rc == 0` (on rc != 0 it calls fsm.fail and returns False). runner.py:492-496 runs stop_record.sh only `if self.started["record"]`. record_d0.sh:72-75 exits 1 when any session is not running or its id is MISSING, and never stops the sessions it did start. Lines 29, 47 and 54 truncate record.pids and delete pid-* without a liveness check. `grep -rn stop_record robosim_eval/ scripts/` shows no other cleanup path.
verification.reasoning:
If one of the six recorders fails its 2 s check, or a pid file is late (MISSING), the other recorder sessions keep running until the record_cap_s (480 s) cap. They keep appending to the failed run's odom.txt, cmd_vel.txt and other streams after result.json is written. In a batch this spans the next attempt's reset and navigation. The ~/robosim_bags bag is never checked or copied.

The runner docstring (line 9, 'TEARDOWN (always: ... stop_record.sh ...)') overstates this. A manual re-run of record_d0.sh on the same dir loses track of the earlier sessions. All recorded runs had record_d0 exit 0, so the path is real but untested and not the normal path.
verification.fix_direction: In teardown, run stop_record.sh whenever record_d0.sh was invoked and record.pids exists, including on rc != 0. Alternatively, have record_d0.sh stop its own started sessions before exiting 1. It should also refuse to start while pid-* sessions in the dir are still alive.

items.title: stop_nav2.sh refuses (exit 5) to stop leftovers of its own launch once the wrapper process has exited, and gives a misleading reason
items.trigger: `ros2 launch` dies abnormally (exception, OOM kill, SIGKILL) while some Nav2 children survive in the session. The wrapper writes nav2.exit and exits, and teardown then calls stop_nav2.sh.
items.expected: The session's leftover processes are recognised as this run's and stopped, or at least the refusal names the real situation and the exit code signals leftovers.
items.actual: alive() is true because members remain, but /proc/$WRAP is gone. starttime_of returns '' and the script records 'start time of process <WRAP> differs from the recorded wrapper start time', then exits 5 without signalling. The Nav2 processes stay. The next start_nav2.sh refuses (exit 3, Nav2 nodes visible), so every remaining batch attempt ends as an error.
items.evidence: Repro (scratch review-wf/shell/repro_stop_nav2_orphans.sh copies stop_nav2.sh lines 24-43 verbatim; a setsid wrapper stand-in records its pid and start time, leaves `sleep 15` behind and exits; nothing is signalled). Output: `wrapper process exists: no; session members: 7282 sleep 15;` then `-> REFUSING to signal session 7280: start time of process 7280 differs from the recorded wrapper start time  (stop_nav2.sh exit 5)`.
items.fix_direction: When /proc/$WRAP no longer exists, check ownership through the surviving members instead. Options: record launch_pid's start time in meta, or check that members' environ/cmdline reference the run dir. If ownership cannot be proven, report 'wrapper exited, N leftover processes in session' with the leftover exit code (1) rather than an identity mismatch.

verification.reasoning:
alive() (pgrep -s) is true because survivors remain in the session. /proc/$WRAP is gone, so starttime_of returns '', which never equals the recorded value. WHY then reports a start-time mismatch rather than 'wrapper exited', and the script exits 5 without signalling anything.

The refusal is conservative, not unsafe. The leftover Nav2 processes and nodes stay, though, and start_nav2.sh:36-37 then refuses (exit 3) on later attempts. The trigger needs `ros2 launch` to die abnormally while children survive, which is an edge case.
verification.fix_direction: When /proc/$WRAP is missing but session members remain, report 'wrapper exited, N leftover processes' with the leftover exit code 1. Optionally prove ownership through the surviving members, for example the recorded launch_pid start time or members' environ/cmdline referencing RUN_DIR, before stopping them.

items.title: send_goal.sh's 330 s client timeout is not a hard bound: `timeout -s INT` has no -k and the CLI client can wait for ever after SIGINT
items.trigger: An accepted goal where the action server stops answering (for example bt_navigator hung) until the 330 s cap sends SIGINT.
items.expected: The header says '124 when the 330 s client timeout fired', which implies the script ends shortly after 330 s.
items.actual: ros2action's send_goal installs a SIGINT handler that calls `rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(node, cancel_future)` with no timeout. After it returns, the result loop continues with no limit because -t is not passed. Without -k, timeout waits for ever, so send_goal.sh blocks indefinitely.
items.evidence: /opt/ros/jazzy/lib/python3.12/site-packages/ros2action/verb/send_goal.py lines 147-170 (handler: `cancel_future = goal_handle.cancel_goal_async(); rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(node, cancel_future)`) and 189-195 (`while rclpy.ok() and not result_future.done(): ... if timeout is not None and elapsed_time >= timeout: break`). Read via a scratch peek script; send_goal.sh itself was not run.
items.fix_direction: Use `timeout -s INT -k 30 330 ...` and record 137 as 'killed after the cap'. Optionally pass `-t` to the client.

verification.repro: Static. I read /opt/ros/jazzy/lib/python3.12/site-packages/ros2action/verb/send_goal.py with scratch peek_sendgoal.sh (MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash .../peek_sendgoal.sh). Lines 147-170 install a SIGINT handler that calls cancel_goal_async() and then `rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(node, cancel_future)` with no timeout. Lines 189-196 loop `while rclpy.ok() and not result_future.done()` and break only if `timeout is not None`, and send_goal.sh:76 does not pass -t. send_goal.sh itself was not run, and no rclpy node was created.
verification.reasoning:
`timeout -s INT 330` without -k sends only SIGINT and then waits for the child indefinitely. If the action server stops answering, the client blocks forever: first in the cancel wait, and afterwards in the result loop, because -t is not passed. send_goal.sh never reaches its end line or exit code. The header's '124 when the 330 s client timeout fired' implies a bounded wait.

Only the D0 manual path uses send_goal.sh (AGENTS.md:48, setup.md:44); the runner uses its own action client. With a responsive server the cancel completes and the script ends with 124 as documented. The trigger needs a hung server, so Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Use `timeout -s INT -k 30 330 ros2 action send_goal ...` and document 137 as 'killed after the cap'. Optionally pass `-t` to the CLI.

items.title: A time-only retry message parsed a few seconds after its displayed minute is pushed to the next day (about 24 h sleep)
items.trigger: Codex prints 'try again at 8:38 AM' when the reset falls later within 08:38, and the queue parses it at 08:38:xx. The same happens when the attempt finishes seconds after the displayed minute.
items.expected: The queue retries about 3 minutes after the displayed time the same day.
items.actual: `$when = $Now.Date.Add(08:38)` is <= Now, so AddDays(1) gives a retry at 08:41 on the next day. test_codex_queue_lib.ps1 has no case for this.
items.evidence: Repro (scratch review-wf/shell/repro_retry.ps1 dot-sources the repo lib): `now=2026-09-30T08:38:20 text=[... try again at 8:38 AM.] -> 2026-10-01T08:41:00`. The same output comes for now=08:39:05. Also shown: lowercase 'am' or a 24 h time returns $null (30 min fallback).
items.fix_direction: Treat a time-only value up to a few minutes in the past as today, and roll to the next day only when it is well in the past. Add fixed-input cases.

verification.repro:
Scratch verify-shell/repro_shell7.ps1 dot-sources the repo codex_queue_lib.ps1 with the text 'ERROR: You've hit your usage limit. ... or try again at 8:38 AM.'. Command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File repro_shell7.ps1. Output:
 now=08:37:50 -> retry 2026-09-30T08:41:00 (sleep 3 min)
 now=08:38:00 -> retry 2026-10-01T08:41:00 (sleep 1443 min)
 now=08:38:20 -> retry 2026-10-01T08:41:00 (sleep 1443 min)
 now=08:41:05 -> retry 2026-10-01T08:41:00 (sleep 1440 min)
verification.reasoning: lib:25-26 builds `$Now.Date.Add(time)` and adds a day whenever the result is <= $Now. A time-only message parsed at or after its displayed minute therefore sleeps about 24 h. That happens when the attempt fails in the same minute as the displayed reset, or when a retry shortly after the displayed time is still limited because of clock skew or rounding. test_codex_queue_lib.ps1 has no such case. The trigger is narrow, so Minor. Fixed on fix/review-round1 @156c31a (10-minute grace), not in HEAD 7fe517e.
verification.fix_direction: Treat a time-only value up to a few minutes in the past as today, and roll to the next day only when it is well in the past. Add fixed-input cases at displayed minute +0 s, +20 s and +3 min.

items.title: A restarted queue overwrites the earlier queue run's attempt files (Move-Item -Force with numbering restarting at 1)
items.trigger: The queue is restarted while a round has codex-<round>-attemptN-* files from an earlier queue run, and the round fails again. Restarts are routine: codex-queue.log shows 5 queue restarts on 2026-09-30.
items.expected: The header says 'A failed attempt keeps its files as codex-<round>-attemptN-{status,stderr,stdout}.txt'. Process evidence is never overwritten (AGENTS.md rule 5).
items.actual: $attempt restarts at 1 in every queue process, and `Move-Item ... -Force` silently replaces the older attempt1..N status/stderr/stdout/report files. The 06:59 log line ('failed round1c-b attempts moved to 2026-09-29-d0/queue-run-20260930-0338/') shows the loss was avoided only by moving files by hand.
items.evidence: Static: lines 70 and 77-81. docs/review/codex-queue.log entries at 06:59:19 and 07:06:13.
items.fix_direction: Continue numbering after the highest existing attemptN, or put the queue start time into the name, and drop -Force.

verification.repro: Scratch verify-shell/repro_shell8.ps1. It creates q8/codex-round1c-c-attempt1-stderr.txt with 'first queue run...' and a fresh codex-round1c-c-stderr.txt. It then runs queue lines 77-80 verbatim with $attempt=1, which is how a restarted queue starts (line 70). Command: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File repro_shell8.ps1. Output: 'codex-round1c-c-attempt1-stderr.txt: second queue run, attempt 1 stderr', so the first run's file was silently replaced.
verification.reasoning:
$attempt restarts at 1 in every queue process, and Move-Item -Force replaces an existing attemptN file. The docs/review/2026-09-29-d0 folder already holds codex-round1c-c-attempt1-{status,stderr,stdout}.txt from queue pid 58748. The queue log shows routine restarts at 00:50, 01:32, 02:36, 06:59, 07:06 and 07:25. The 06:59 entry records moving earlier attempt files by hand to avoid exactly this.

This contradicts the header ('A failed attempt keeps its files') and AGENTS.md rule 4/5 (do not overwrite; evidence is fact). Fixed on 156c31a (numbering continues after existing files, -Force dropped), not in HEAD.
verification.fix_direction: Continue numbering after the highest existing attemptN, or include the queue start time in the name. Drop -Force so a collision fails loudly.

items.title: The queue lock checks only whether some process has the recorded PID, is not atomic, and does not see an orphaned runner left by a killed queue
items.trigger: (a) A queue is stopped by killing it during a round, as the log shows is done to requeue ('queue pid ... stopped by Claude'). Its child `powershell -File run_codex_review.ps1` / `cmd /c codex exec` keeps running, and the next queue finds the PID dead, takes the lock and starts the same round. (b) A stale lock whose PID Windows has reused for an unrelated process. (c) Two starts interleave between Test-Path and Out-File.
items.expected: 'Only one queue runs at a time', and no two Codex runs write the same round's files.
items.actual: (a) Two codex runs write the same codex-<round>-{report,stdout,stderr,status} paths, and the attempt/limit classification then reads mixed files. (b) The queue exits 3 on every start (only the log says why) until the lock is deleted by hand. (c) Both queues run, and the first one's `finally` deletes the lock the other believes it holds.
items.evidence: Static: lines 54-60 (owner = first line of the lock file, alive = Get-Process -Id), line 60 (non-atomic write), line 91 (unconditional Remove-Item). codex-queue.log shows repeated kill-and-restart at 00:50, 01:32, 02:36 and 07:06.
items.fix_direction: Create the lock atomically (FileMode.CreateNew). Store PID plus process start time plus script path, and verify all of them. At start, refuse while a run_codex_review.ps1/codex process for the same Dir/round is still running.

verification.repro: Part (b) was reproduced. Scratch verify-shell/repro_shell9.ps1 writes a scratch lock holding the PID of an unrelated live process (explorer.exe, standing in for a reused PID) and runs queue lines 54-59 verbatim. Output: 'refuse: another queue (pid 11364) holds ...q9.lock -> exit 3 (pid 11364 is explorer)', exit=3. Parts (a) and (c) are static.
verification.reasoning:
Lines 54-59 treat any live process with the recorded PID as the owner. There is no start time or command-line check, so a reused PID blocks every start until someone deletes the lock (b). Test-Path followed by Out-File is not atomic, and the finally block at line 91 removes the lock unconditionally (c). That race needs two simultaneous starts, which is unlikely.

For (a): killing the queue does not kill its `powershell -File run_codex_review.ps1` / `cmd /c codex exec` child, because Windows does not cascade TerminateProcess. The lock then points to a dead PID, and a restarted queue would launch the same round, since the report is written only at the end. I did not verify whether the second run's Start-Process redirect then shares or fails on the files still held open by the first run.

All recorded kills (00:50, 01:32, 02:36, 07:06, 07:25) happened during NotBefore or usage-limit sleeps, so no orphan has occurred yet. The practical risk is small.
verification.fix_direction: Create the lock with FileMode.CreateNew. Store PID, process start time and script path, and verify all of them. At start, refuse while a run_codex_review.ps1 or codex process for the same Dir/round is still alive. In finally, remove the lock only if it still names this process.

items.title: Run from another checkout, the fake-node tests exercise /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval's doctor, not the checkout under test
items.trigger: test_runner_fake.sh or test_doctor_fake.sh is run from a git worktree. Commit 67a8ffa changed test_runner_fake's REPO to 'the checkout this script is in', and docs/plan.md:42 records moving development into a worktree during batches.
items.expected: Every component a fake test exercises comes from the checkout being tested.
items.actual: The runner is imported from the worktree, but its doctor step calls the worktree's doctor.sh, which does `cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval` and `python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor`, so the main checkout's doctor runs. test_doctor_fake.sh hard-codes REPO=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval and does the same. A doctor change under test is never exercised, and a PASS can come from different code.
items.evidence: Static: test_runner_fake.sh:13 (REPO from BASH_SOURCE) versus doctor.sh:13/21-22 and test_doctor_fake.sh:12/23 (hard-coded REPO, cd, python3 -m). `git show 67a8ffa -- scripts/wsl/test_runner_fake.sh` shows the REPO change.
items.fix_direction: Derive REPO from BASH_SOURCE in doctor.sh and test_doctor_fake.sh (and the other wrappers), or make the tests assert the module path they imported.

verification.repro:
Scratch verify-shell/repro_shell10.sh uses the existing worktree scratchpad/wt-fix (fix/review-round1 @156c31a, from `git worktree list`). It mirrors the module resolution with importlib find_spec only, with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and nothing run. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash .../verify-shell/repro_shell10.sh. Output:
 worktree doctor.sh REPO line: 13:REPO=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval
 runner (test_runner_fake cwd=worktree): .../scratchpad/wt-fix/robosim_eval/runner.py
 doctor (doctor.sh cwd=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval): /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval/robosim_eval/doctor.py
 runner WSL dir -> doctor.sh used: .../scratchpad/wt-fix/scripts/wsl/doctor.sh
verification.reasoning:
test_runner_fake.sh:13 derives REPO from BASH_SOURCE and runs the worktree's runner. The runner's WSL constant (runner.py:37-38) is derived from its own file, and the runner calls that doctor.sh on every fake case: PREPARE runs it even with --no-sim (runner.py:206-210). doctor.sh:13/21-22 hard-codes REPO=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval, cds there and runs `python3 -m robosim_eval.doctor`, which resolves to the main checkout's module. test_doctor_fake.sh:12 hard-codes the same path.

A worktree is in real use: wt-fix exists, and plan.md:42 records worktree development during batches. So a fake-test PASS in a worktree can come from a different doctor than the one under test. Weak test isolation, Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Derive REPO from BASH_SOURCE in doctor.sh, test_doctor_fake.sh and the other wrappers that the runner calls, or let the runner pass its REPO through the environment. Have the fake tests log and assert the imported module paths.

items.title: Ctrl-C does not reach the runner with the documented command; the documented exit-20 'Ctrl-C' behaviour was never tested this way
items.trigger: An operator follows README step 2 (`wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -l .../run_scenario.sh normal ...` in a terminal) and presses Ctrl-C during navigation.
items.expected: README.md:41 says '20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断(已取消目标并收尾)'. setup.md:81 says 'Ctrl-C 只会让它取消目标并照常收尾'. technical-overview §15 (D2 row) says '导航中 Ctrl-C → 取消、停车、收尾'.
items.actual: run_scenario.sh (and run_batch.sh, doctor.sh) run the Python process under `timeout` without `--foreground`. Inside a non-interactive script, GNU timeout calls setpgid(0,0) and moves itself and the runner out of the terminal's foreground process group, so the SIGINT from a terminal Ctrl-C only reaches bash. The runner keeps navigating until its normal end (up to the 300 s wall limit plus teardown) and exits 0/10/11, not 20. The D2 evidence (runs/normal-20260930-004634) came from a scratch script sending SIGINT. The fake test (test_runner_fake.sh:49) sends `kill -INT` straight to the Python PID. Neither path goes through the documented terminal/timeout path, so this is untested.
items.evidence: I reproduced it in WSL (bash 5.2.21, coreutils timeout 9.4) with a scratch copy of run_scenario.sh's shape (`set -uo pipefail; cd; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout -s INT -k 5 8 python3 -c <SIGINT handler>` as the last line), started as `bash -l script` under a fresh pty, with ^C typed after 1.5 s: output 'child: no SIGINT within 6 s -> run continued, exit 0'. The same script with `timeout --foreground` gave 'child: SIGINT received 1.44 s after start' and exit 20. Files: scratchpad/review-wf/docs/fake_run_scenario_last.sh, fake_run_scenario_fg.sh, pty_ctrl_c.py. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -c "cd <scratch> && python3 pty_ctrl_c.py <scratch>/fake_run_scenario_last.sh". Assumption: wsl.exe passes a console Ctrl-C to the Linux pty as ^C (normal WSL interactive behaviour); I did not press Ctrl-C in a real Windows console.
items.fix_direction: Either run the Python process with `timeout --foreground` (keeping the cap semantics in mind) or forward SIGINT/SIGTERM from the script to timeout. Then verify with a real Ctrl-C on the documented command and record it. Until then, correct the README/setup/overview wording (the interrupt was sent by kill -INT to the process, not by Ctrl-C).

verification.repro: Scratch files under scratchpad/review-wf/verify-docs/: child.py (installs a SIGINT handler, exits 20 on SIGINT, else exits 0 after 6 s); shape_nofg.sh (same shape as run_scenario.sh:10-20: set -uo pipefail; cd; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout -s INT -k 5 8 python3 child.py); shape_fg.sh (same with timeout --foreground); pty_ctrlc.py (pty.fork -> exec 'bash -l <script>', writes ^C to the pty master after 1.5 s, waits). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -c "cd $S && python3 pty_ctrlc.py $S/shape_nofg.sh; python3 pty_ctrlc.py $S/shape_fg.sh". Output: '^Cchild: no SIGINT within 6 s -> run continued, exit 0 / script exitcode: 0 elapsed 6.1s' and then '^Cchild: SIGINT received 1.44 s after start -> exit 20 / script exitcode: 20 elapsed 1.5s' (coreutils timeout 9.4, bash 5.2.21).
verification.reasoning: run_scenario.sh:20, run_batch.sh:16 and doctor.sh:22 start Python under 'timeout' without --foreground. GNU timeout then calls setpgid(0,0) and moves itself and the child out of the terminal's foreground process group; the coreutils man page says only --foreground lets the command 'get TTY signals'. A pty ^C therefore sends SIGINT only to the script's bash. Non-interactive bash waits for the child and does not forward the signal, so the runner keeps navigating and exits with its normal code (0/10/11), not 20. The pty reproduction shows exactly this, and --foreground restores delivery. The documented behaviour (README:41 '20 = 被 Ctrl-C 中断(已取消目标并收尾)', setup.md:81 'Ctrl-C 只会让它取消目标并照常收尾', technical-overview.md:403/:439 'D2 … 导航中 Ctrl-C → 取消') was never exercised on this path. I did not press Ctrl-C in a real Windows console, because that would require a visible console on a live system.
verification.fix_direction: Use 'timeout --foreground' (accepting that grandchildren are then not capped), or trap INT/TERM in the scripts and forward them to the timeout/runner PID. critic.coverage:
What I examined, beyond the seven dimension reports (read-only; scratch files in scratchpad/review-wf/critic).

(a) Cross-module data flow. I traced every result.json field back to its source:
- runner facts: terminal status, error_code, stop_confirmed, cancel and timeout reasons, clock_backward (runner /clock subscription, reset at WAIT_READY).
- sim_control ground truth: at_stop and at_end.
- Kit contact monitor: found_pairs from FOUND events between the post-spawn clear fetch and the teardown fetch.
- analyser data_integrity: bag receive time over [bag accept, bag stop-confirm].
- Top-level timing, nav2_raw and stop_still: analyser (bag plus runner transcript).
- Report: outcome, validation, safety and data from the evaluator; time, Nav2 status, error and recoveries from the analyser; reset error from events.jsonl.
- Time bases: I checked sim vs wall stamps in the runner tracker (odom header vs /clock), the analyser (rosbag receive time is wall because no --use-sim-time is set), the evaluator (dropout in wall seconds) and the report (analyser sim seconds). Stream-name contracts: config required/informational names equal the analyser keys. Goal and transcript formats: runner str(float) and Transcript both parse. Found: critic-2, critic-3, critic-7; critic-1 comes from shared state (sim reset and the contact buffer) across processes.

items.title: A second runner resets the live simulation and empties the shared contact buffer before anything detects the run already in progress
items.trigger: A run or batch is navigating (for example the ~27 min README step-3 batch), and the user starts `run_scenario.sh normal` or a second `run_batch.sh` in another PowerShell. A second trigger: the manual `isaac_py.ps1 ... -Call 'robosim_contacts_fetch(True)'` documented in artifacts/d3/commands.md:12, run during a run.
items.expected: The second invocation should refuse before touching shared simulator state (reset, spawn, contact buffer), following the same 'never two instances' rule that start_nav2.sh applies to Nav2. A contact read that another run depends on should not be destructive.
items.actual: PREPARE runs sim.reset() on the other run's live simulation: /clock restarts at 0 and the robot is teleported to the spawn while its Nav2 goal is still active. It then deletes and respawns obstacles and calls contacts.fetch(), which clears the Kit buffer. Only after all that does start_nav2.sh refuse (exit 3). That gives runner exit 30, not 31, so a second batch repeats the reset on every attempt. The second runner's teardown fetch clears the buffer once more. The first run loses every contact event recorded before the last fetch, so its safety_status can be 'pass' and the report can show 'collisions 0' after a real collision. Its data also becomes incomplete because of the clock jump. Neither robosim_eval nor run_*.sh has any lock (grep found none).
items.evidence: repro_concurrent_prepare.py drives the real Runner._prepare/_wait_ready with recording stubs (no ROS). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 .../review-wf/critic/repro_concurrent_prepare.py .../review-wf/critic". Output in order: write_manifest, write_resolved_config, sim.get_state, sim.entity_state, contacts.install, 'sim.reset <-- live simulation of the OTHER run is reset', sim.entity_state, 'sim.spawn_box box_1', 'contacts.fetch <-- clears the monitor buffer the OTHER run will read at its teardown', 'script doctor.sh -> exit 0', 'script start_nav2.sh -> exit 3 (refused: Nav2 of the other run is running)', then 'execution_status: error errors: ['start_nav2.sh exit 3'] abort_batch: False exit would be 30'. contact_monitor.py:124-132: fetch(clear=True) clears events, persist counts and the dropped count. start_nav2.sh:26-38 holds the only duplicate check.
items.fix_direction: Take a host-wide exclusive lock (flock on a fixed file) in runner.main and batch.main before PREPARE, and check for a running carter_navigation launch or Nav2 nodes before any sim_control call. Make the contact fetch non-destructive: give each run its own cursor or run token, so a diagnostic read or another process cannot drain a run's events.

verification.repro: Scratch file C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\d--RoboSim-Eval\59900d3e-5384-418b-8374-e6a8773582da\scratchpad\review-wf\verify-critic\v1_concurrent.py. It executes the real Kit-side robosim_eval/kit/contact_monitor.py against fake omni/pxr modules, routes contacts._call in-process, and drives the real Runner._prepare, _wait_ready and _teardown of a second 'normal' run. Sim is stubbed and start_nav2.sh returns 3. It then runs the first run's teardown fetch and the real evaluate_run. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/c/.../review-wf/verify-critic/v1_concurrent.py /mnt/c/.../review-wf/verify-critic". Output: 'Kit buffer before run 2: 1 event(s)' / 'run2: sim.reset (other run's world ...)' / 'run2: contacts.fetch drained 1 event(s)' / 'run2: doctor.sh -> 0' / 'run2: start_nav2.sh -> 3' / 'run2: contacts.fetch drained 0 event(s)' / 'run2 exit: 30 ['start_nav2.sh exit 3']' / 'run 1 teardown fetch: 0 event(s)' / 'run 1 (collision scenario, clock_backward_jumps=0): safety=pass validation=pass disallowed=0' / 'run 1 (collision scenario, clock_backward_jumps=1): safety=pass validation=inconclusive reasons=['data incomplete: /clock jumped backwards 1 time(s) during the run']'.
verification.reasoning:
The code at HEAD matches the finding. Runner._prepare calls _reset_sim (runner.py:203-205) before anything checks whether another run is active. _reset_sim installs contacts, calls sim.reset(), spawns obstacles and calls contact_client.fetch() (240-277). The reset is 'stop, delete spawned entities, Play', with /clock restarting at 0 (technical-overview.md:386). fetch() clears the shared Kit buffer (contact_monitor.py:61-69; contacts.py:53-58). The only duplicate check is in start_nav2.sh:62-74, which runs only in _wait_ready. The refusal gives execution error with abort_batch false, so exit 30, and batch.py:61 aborts only on 31. A second batch therefore resets the live simulation on every attempt. I found no lock in robosim_eval/ or scripts/.

Mitigating detail: if the first run is EXECUTING when the reset hits, its /clock backward counter (runner.py:83-84) and the bag's backward stamps make it inconclusive, not pass. Even then it keeps safety_status 'pass' and collisions 0 although its contact events were drained. A5 says lost contact data must never read as a safety pass.

A wrong pass is still reachable. Suppose the second run's reset lands in the first run's PREPARE/doctor or start_nav2 window. The first run does not spin while doctor.sh and start_nav2.sh run. clock_backward is zeroed at _wait_ready start (283), and the bag starts only at SEND_GOAL. So a jump whose new timeline has already passed the old value goes unnoticed. Meanwhile the first run's obstacle has been deleted, or the other scenario's obstacle spawned. A bypass run can then pass with no box, or a normal run can fail on someone else's low_box.

This needs an operator mistake, but a plausible one: a 27 min batch, with no warning in README. The project guards a second Isaac and a second Nav2, and this is the gap. The commands.md:12 trigger is weak: it is a historical diagnostic record, not an instruction.
verification.fix_direction: Take an exclusive host-wide lock (flock on a fixed path) in runner.main and batch.main before PREPARE. Also move the 'Nav2 or carter_navigation launch already running' check, or a doctor-level equivalent, ahead of any sim_control call. Make an in-progress refusal exit 31, so a batch stops instead of repeating resets. Give the contact buffer a per-run token or cursor so another process cannot drain a run's events.

items.title: Teardown step failures never reach execution_status, the verdict, the exit code or the batch; a failed offline analysis is reported as 'stream: no data'
items.trigger: stop_nav2.sh exits 1 (Nav2 nodes remain), 5 (ownership refused, see shell-5) or 124 (180 s script cap). Or stop_record.sh exits 4 (a recorder exit code is missing) or 6 (a required topic recorded 0 messages). Or analyze_attempt.sh exits 1 (bag unreadable) or 2 (goal mismatch).
items.expected: A run whose resident processes were not stopped, or whose recording or analysis failed, should not end 'completed' with a clean exit (A5: execution_status means the run flow was complete; A7: resident processes are judged by their real exit codes). The reason should name the failed step. A batch should not continue into guaranteed failures.
items.actual: The codes are only stored in runner.exit_codes. With stop_nav2 1, 5 or 124, or stop_record 4 or 6, the run is execution_status completed, validation pass, exit 0. The batch continues, and every later attempt fails at start_nav2.sh (exit 3, i.e. runner 30) while the old Nav2 keeps running. With analyze exit 1 or 2 the reasons read 'data incomplete: clock: no data; odom: no data; tf_odom_base: no data'. The result.analyzer block then holds placeholder 'inconclusive/incomplete' values although no analyser ran.
items.evidence: repro_teardown_codes.py drives the real Runner._teardown -> _write_result -> _evaluate -> _exit_code with stubbed scripts and a complete analyser data_integrity. Output: {stop_nav2.sh:1} -> execution_status completed, validation pass, runner_exit 0; {stop_nav2.sh:124} -> completed/pass/0; {stop_record.sh:6} -> completed/pass/0; {stop_record.sh:4} -> completed/pass/0. repro_teardown_codes2.py: {analyze_attempt.sh:2} and {analyze_attempt.sh:1} -> inconclusive, reasons ['data incomplete: clock: no data; odom: no data; tf_odom_base: no data'], runner_exit 11. In all 31 recorded real runs these codes were 0, so this path has not happened yet.
items.fix_direction: Pass the teardown exit codes into the evaluator as execution problems. When stop_nav2 or stop_record could not stop their processes, return an error that aborts the batch. Report 'offline analysis failed (exit N)' instead of per-stream 'no data', and leave result.analyzer out when the analyser did not produce a result.

verification.repro: Scratch file v2_teardown.py in review-wf/verify-critic. It drives the real Runner._teardown, _write_result, _evaluate and _exit_code with stubbed scripts and with the analyser writing complete data_integrity (except in the analyze-failure cases). Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/c/.../verify-critic/v2_teardown.py /mnt/c/.../verify-critic". Output: {stop_nav2.sh:1} exec completed, valid pass, exit 0. {stop_nav2.sh:5} completed/pass/0. {stop_nav2.sh:124} completed/pass/0. {stop_record.sh:4} completed/pass/0. {analyze_attempt.sh:2} completed, inconclusive, reasons ['data incomplete: clock: no data; odom: no data; tf_odom_base: no data'], analyzer_block {task_outcome unknown, safety unknown, data incomplete, validation inconclusive}, exit 11. {analyze_attempt.sh:1} gives the same.
verification.reasoning:
The teardown codes are stored only in facts['exit_codes'] (runner.py:495, 499-502, 504). _evaluate never reads them, and _exit_code (560-565) depends only on fsm.execution_status and validation_status. docs/setup.md:86 documents exit 0/10/11 as '流程完整' (flow complete), which is false when stop_nav2 leaves Nav2 running (exit 1, 5 or 124). The batch continues because only 31 aborts (batch.py:61). The next start_nav2.sh then refuses (exit 3), and every later attempt ends at 30.

When analyze_attempt.py returns 1 or 2 it writes no result.json (analyze_attempt.py:415-426). _write_result then uses the placeholder dict, so integ is {} and every required stream reads 'no data'. That reason is misleading, although result.schema does say 'no offline analysis'.

The verdict direction stays safe for analyse failures (inconclusive), and the codes are kept in result.json and events.jsonl. None of these paths occurred in the recorded runs. No test covers teardown exit codes. Minor is the right grade.
verification.fix_direction: Feed the stop_nav2 and stop_record exit codes into the verdict as execution problems. Abort the batch (31) when Nav2 or the recorders could not be confirmed stopped. When analyze exits 1 or 2, report 'offline analysis failed (exit N)' and leave out the placeholder analyzer block.

items.title: The 'mean time (success only)' basis label counts only reached runs that have analyser timing, so it misstates how many runs reached
items.trigger: A batch where one reached run has no analyser timing: the analyser failed or no bag was copied, while the D3 evaluator still gives task_outcome 'reached' from runner facts and ground truth.
items.expected: The label says how many reached runs exist and how many of them have a time. For example: 3 reached, mean over 2 with timing.
items.actual: The run is dropped silently and the label reads 'reached runs only (2 of 3)'. The report looks as if only 2 of the 3 runs reached, while the outcome column shows reached 3.
items.evidence: repro_mean_basis.py builds 3 reached runs, one without a 'timing' block, and calls load_runs and summarize. Output: {'attempts': 3, 'outcome': {'reached': 3}, 'mean_accept_to_result_sim_s_success_only': 16.5, 'mean_basis': 'reached runs only (2 of 3)'}.
items.fix_direction: Count reached runs separately from reached runs that have timing, for example 'reached 3 of 3; mean over the 2 with timing'. Or show the time as missing for the run instead of dropping it.

verification.repro: Scratch file v3_mean.py in review-wf/verify-critic builds 3 reached 'normal' runs; the third has no 'timing' block. It calls load_runs, summarize and render_html. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc "cd /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/c/.../verify-critic/v3_mean.py /mnt/c/.../verify-critic". Output: {'attempts': 3, 'outcome': {'reached': 3}, 'mean_accept_to_result_sim_s_success_only': 16.5, 'mean_basis': 'reached runs only (2 of 3)'}.
verification.reasoning:
report.py:101 keeps only reached runs whose accept_to_result_sim_s is not None, and line 107 prints len(reached) out of len(rs). tests/test_report.py:55 shows the label is meant to read '(reached count) of (attempts)'. A reached run without timing is therefore shown as if it had not reached.

This is reachable: the D3 evaluator gives 'reached' from runner facts and ground truth even when the analyser failed (see critic-2), or when timing.accept_to_result_sim_s is None (analyze_attempt.py:373). The table cell also shows 'reached 3' in the outcome column, which makes the inconsistency visible. It is a small report inaccuracy.
verification.fix_direction: Label the mean with both counts, for example 'mean over 2 reached runs with timing; 3 reached of 3'. Or show the run's time as missing instead of dropping it silently.

items.trigger: Following the README prerequisites (also docs/setup.md:11-12, which says the scripts may be re-run): running `install_ros2_jazzy.sh` or `setup_workspace.sh` on this checkout or another machine.
items.expected: Re-running setup should leave the recorded D0b product evidence (A7: command, exit code, log per verification) unchanged, or write to a new location.
items.actual: install_ros2_jazzy.sh:20-24 tees to /mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval/artifacts/d0b/install-jazzy.log (-a) and overwrites install-jazzy.exit. setup_workspace.sh:13-19 does the same with setup-workspace.log and .exit by default. The ROBOSIM_SETUP_LOG override exists but README does not use it. All four files are tracked, so a failed re-run replaces the recorded exit 0 of the original D0b install.
items.evidence: git ls-files artifacts/d0b lists install-jazzy.exit, install-jazzy.log, setup-workspace.exit and setup-workspace.log. Script lines are cited above. Not executed: it needs sudo and installation.
items.fix_direction: Write setup logs to a timestamped path outside the tracked evidence by default, for example artifacts/setup-<time>/ or a temp directory. Or use ROBOSIM_SETUP_LOG in README and docs/setup.md.

verification.repro: Not executed (needs sudo and would write to the repository). Code evidence: install_ros2_jazzy.sh:20-24 has fixed LOG_DIR=/mnt/d/RoboSim-Eval/artifacts/d0b, then exec > >(tee -a install-jazzy.log), and its EXIT trap overwrites install-jazzy.exit. setup_workspace.sh:13-19 defaults LOG to artifacts/d0b/setup-workspace.log (tee -a) and overwrites the .exit file. Its only override is ROBOSIM_SETUP_LOG, and line 15's comment says 'override to re-run without touching D0b evidence'. git ls-files artifacts/d0b lists install-jazzy.exit/.log and setup-workspace.exit/.log as tracked. README.md:14-15 and docs/setup.md:11-12 ('可重跑') give the commands without the override.
