The originals survive in git history, so nothing is irrecoverably lost. The harm is that tracked evidence becomes modified or mixed: another machine's log gets appended, or a failed re-run overwrites the exit 0. As a side effect, later runs' manifests show dirty_tracked_files true. Re-running is rare, which makes this Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Default the setup logs to a new timestamped location outside the tracked D0b evidence, or use ROBOSIM_SETUP_LOG (and an equivalent for install_ros2_jazzy.sh) in README and docs/setup.md.

items.title: manifest.json digests do not identify what the run actually loaded
items.trigger: Any run where the vendor source tree and the colcon install copy differ, for example after a vendor checkout change without a rebuild. Also a change to the remote world USD, or untracked code or config files in use.
items.expected: A6 manifest: asset, map and configuration digests of what was actually used, and a dirty flag that detects local modifications.
items.actual: write_manifest hashes VENDOR_PKG = the src/ tree. start_nav2.sh launches with $(find-pkg-share carter_navigation), which is install/share, and setup_workspace.sh:67 builds without --symlink-install, so these are separate copies. nav2_params.write_params also derives the D5 file from the src copy, so normal (install copy) and normal_slow (derived from src) can differ by more than the declared change while both digests claim the same base. The world_uri (a remote S3 USD) has no digest. dirty_tracked_files uses --untracked-files=no, so untracked modules or configs do not mark the run dirty (README.md:64 says 'whether there are uncommitted changes').
items.evidence: vendor_cmp.sh (read-only, WSL): the src and install sha256 values are identical today (params 8349fe3b..., map yaml 05263f31..., png dd2f5e38...), so the gap is latent. The vendor launch file line 5 shows params_file default=$(find-pkg-share carter_navigation)/params/carter_navigation_params.yaml. The D5 manifest (artifacts/d5/batch-20260930-021530/runs/normal-20260930-021530/manifest.json) has no world or obstacle asset digest.
items.fix_direction: Hash the files from `ros2 pkg prefix carter_navigation`/share, which are the ones Nav2 loads, and derive the D5 params from that copy. Record the world URI together with a digest or ETag when available. Include untracked files in the dirty check, or list them.

verification.repro: Scratch file v6_vendor.sh in review-wf/verify-critic, read-only. Command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash /mnt/c/.../verify-critic/v6_vendor.sh. Output: install/share/carter_navigation/params/carter_navigation_params.yaml and the map yaml are regular files (-rw-r--r--, readlink -f resolves to themselves), not symlinks into src. The sha256 values of src and install are identical today: params 8349fe3ba9d8, map yaml 05263f31a87e, png dd2f5e382a5f, launch 7071bcad5469. The install launch line 5 has params_file default=$(find-pkg-share carter_navigation)/params/carter_navigation_params.yaml. The D5 manifest artifacts/d5/batch-20260930-021530/runs/normal-20260930-021530/manifest.json has digests config, map_yaml, map_image and nav2_params only: no world or asset digest.
verification.reasoning:
run_io.py:23 has VENDOR_PKG = the src tree, and write_manifest (76-78) hashes the src copies. Nav2 loads the install/share copies, which are separate regular files because setup_workspace.sh:67 builds without --symlink-install. runner.py:191 also derives the D5 params from the src copy. That gap is latent: the files are identical today, and diverging them would take a violation of the 'do not modify the vendor workspace' rule or a stale build.

The real A6 gap is different. A6 asks for 资产/地图/配置摘要 (asset, map and config digests), yet the world USD (a remote S3 URI, whose path is versioned 6.1) has no digest in the manifest; only the URI appears in config.resolved.yaml. The obstacle assets are tracked in git, so the commit covers them.

The dirty flag uses --untracked-files=no (run_io.py:64). The key is honestly named dirty_tracked_files, but README.md:64 describes it as '是否有未提交改动' (whether there are uncommitted changes). This is a small reproducibility and doc gap, Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Hash the files under `ros2 pkg prefix carter_navigation`/share (what Nav2 loads) and derive the D5 params from that copy. Record the world URI in the manifest, with an ETag or digest when obtainable. Either list untracked files or reword README to 'tracked files modified'.

items.title: README misdescribes two outputs: summary.json is not 'the same content' as report.html, and trajectory.csv is not only an odometry trajectory
items.trigger: A reader uses summary.json as the machine-readable report, or reads trajectory.csv as odometry per README.
items.expected: The README describes the files as report.py and analyze_attempt.py actually write them.
items.actual: report.py:234 writes summary.json = summarize(runs), i.e. per-scenario aggregates only. It has no per-run rows, no failure list with reasons, no commits or versions, and no trajectories, all of which report.html contains. trajectory.csv (analyze_attempt.py:388-397) mixes four sources: ideal odometry, odometry plus spawn, AMCL tf estimate, and Nav2 feedback (AMCL-based). They are told apart only by the 'source' column, and speeds exist only on odometry rows. README line 63 calls it '里程计轨迹(仿真时间戳、位置、速度)', i.e. an odometry trajectory.
items.evidence: Code lines are cited above. The tracked artifacts/d4/batch-20260930-013010/runs/summary.json holds only the per-scenario dict.
items.fix_direction: Correct the README rows: summary.json holds per-scenario aggregates, and trajectory.csv holds several position sources marked by the source column, including AMCL estimates. Or write the per-run table into summary.json.

verification.repro: Read the recorded artifacts. head of artifacts/d4/batch-20260930-013010/runs/summary.json shows only per-scenario aggregates (attempts, validation/outcome/safety/data counts, mean_accept_to_result_sim_s_success_only, mean_basis, max_arrival_error_m, collisions, runs_with_nav2_recoveries, max_reset_error_m). The source column of a normal run's trajectory.csv in that batch has 4 sources: 3360 'ideal odometry /chassis/odom', 3360 'sim_state_odom_plus_spawn', 3360 'tf map->odom (AMCL) + odom->base_link (estimate)' and 15021 'nav2_feedback of the target goal (map, AMCL-based estimate)'. Speeds are filled only on the odometry rows.
verification.reasoning:
report.py:234 writes summary.json = summarize(runs), which holds aggregates only. report.html (render_html, 170-221) also has the per-run table, the failure and inconclusive list with reasons, commits and versions, and the trajectory map. README.md:49's '同样内容的机器可读版' (a machine-readable version of the same content) is therefore inaccurate.

analyze_attempt.py:388-397 writes four position sources in two frames (odom and map), including AMCL estimates. README.md:63's '里程计轨迹(仿真时间戳、位置、速度)' (odometry trajectory: sim timestamps, positions, speeds) is incomplete. A reader who does not filter on the source column would mix frames and sources. The file itself satisfies A6 (frame and source marked); only the README description is wrong. That is a small doc inaccuracy, Minor.
verification.fix_direction: Correct the README rows. summary.json holds per-scenario aggregates, with per-run details in each result.json and report.html. trajectory.csv holds several position sources (odometry, odometry plus spawn, AMCL estimate, Nav2 feedback), marked by the frame_id and source columns. Alternatively, add the per-run table to summary.json.
